ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r1.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r1.claim: He explains ribāṭ as waiting for one prayer after another and says there was no military frontier post in the Prophet’s time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r1.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: الرباط انتظارا الصلاة بعد الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r2.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r2.claim: He adduces the Prophet’s report that ablution despite hardship, walking to mosques, and awaiting the next prayer erase sins and raise ranks; it calls this ribāṭ three times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r2.anchor: إسباغ الوضوء على المكاره وكثرة الخطا إلى المساجد وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة فذلكم الرباط ثلاثا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r3.claim: He says the correct lexical and legal meaning is remaining on the frontier for God, originally tied to horses; a frontier guard may be mounted or on foot.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r3.anchor: والقول الصحيح هو أن الرباط هو الملازمة في سبيل الله، أصلها من ربط الخيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r4.claim: The prayer-waiting report only compares prayer-waiting with frontier service, since it too is a saving path; the literal meaning of ribāṭ is the frontier post.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r4.anchor: إنما هو تشبيه بالرباط في سبيل الله، إذ انتظار الصلاة إنما هو سبيل من السبل المنجية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r5.speaker: ابن المواز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r5.claim: Jurists define a murābiṭ as someone who travels to a frontier post and remains there for a period; permanent local residents who work there are not technically murābiṭūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r5.anchor: المرابط في سبيل الله عند الفقهاء هو الذي يشخص إلى ثغر من الثغور ليرابط فيه مدة ما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r6.claim: He explains ṣābirū as matching or surpassing the enemy in patience and endurance under the hardships of battle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r6.anchor: غالبوهم في الصبر على شدائد الحرب، لا تكونوا أقل صبرا منهم وثباتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r7.claim: He says the command to persist at the frontier follows the general command to be patient to stress the greater difficulty of this particular endurance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r7.anchor: والمصابرة باب من الصبر، ذكر بعد الصبر على ما يجب الصبر عليه تحقيقا لشدته وصعوبته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r8.claim: He reads rābiṭū as stationing horses at frontier posts, watchful and prepared to fight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r8.anchor: وأقيموا في الثغور رباطين خيلكم فيها مترصدين مستعدين للغزو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r9.claim: A Prophetic report promises that a day and night of frontier service equals a month of fasting and prayer, without breaking the fast or leaving prayer except for need.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p485/r9.anchor: من رابط يوما وليلة في سبيل الله كان كعدل صيام شهر وقيامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r1.claim: Muslim’s report says a day and night of frontier service is better than the world and its contents, and the guard’s provision and safety from the grave’s testers continue after death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r1.anchor: رباط يوم وليلة خير من صيام شهر وقيامه وإن مات جرى عليه رزقه وأمن الفتان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r2.claim: Abū Dāwūd’s report says other people’s deeds end at death, while a frontier guard’s deeds keep growing until the Resurrection and he is protected from the grave’s testers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p486/r2.anchor: كل الميت يختم على عمله إلا المرابط فإنه ينمو له عمله إلى يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r1.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r1.claim: Abu Salama interprets this verse’s ribat as waiting for one prayer after another, noting there were no military frontiers to guard in the Prophet’s time.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r1.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن هذه الآية في انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة،

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r2.claim: The Prophet describes ablution through hardship, walking to mosques, and waiting for the next prayer as acts that erase sins and raise ranks, calling them ribat three times.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r2.anchor: وكثرة الخطا إلى المساجد وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة فذلكم الرباط

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya holds that ribat properly means remaining in God’s path at a frontier; the prayer hadith compares waiting to military ribat.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r3.anchor: والقول الصحيح هو أن الرباط هو الملازمة في سبيل الله

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r4.claim: Qurtubi rejects Ibn Atiyya’s restriction of the lexical meaning: al-Khalil says ribat also means keeping to prayer, so waiting for prayer is literally ribat.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r4.anchor: فإن الخليل بن أحمد أحد أئمة اللغة وثقاتها قد قال: الرباط ملازمة الثغور،

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r5.speaker: الشيباني
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r5.claim: Al-Shaybani’s description of enduring water as murabit, reported by Ibn Faris, supports a broad lexical sense of something held in place.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r5.anchor: أنه يقال: ماء مترابط أي دائم لا ينزح حكاه ابن فارس

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r6.claim: Ribat is binding something so it does not loosen; it disciplines the heart in good intention and the body in obedience, especially through horses at the frontier and constancy in prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r6.anchor: فإن المرابطة عند العرب: العقد على الشيء حتى لا ينحل،

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة وجابر وعلي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r7.claim: Reports from Abu Hurayra, Jabir, and Ali apply the Prophet’s term ribat to keeping oneself attached to the prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r7.anchor: وارتباط النفس على الصلوات كما قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رواه أبو هريرة وجابر وعلي

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r8.speaker: محمد بن المواز
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r8.claim: For jurists, a murabit is one who travels to a frontier and stays there for a period to guard it.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r8.anchor: هو الذي يشخص إلى ثغر من الثغور ليرابط فيه مدة ما قاله محمد بن المواز

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya distinguishes permanent frontier residents who live and earn there with families: they protect the border but are not technically murabitun.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r9.anchor: فهم وإن كانوا حماة فليسوا بمرابطين. قاله ابن عطية

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r10.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r10.claim: Ibn Khuzaymandad permits families at a secure, fortified frontier; at an unsafe frontier a qualified fighter may guard personally but should not bring family liable to capture.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r10.anchor: حالة يكون الثغر مأمونا منيعا يجوز سكناه بالأهل والولد. وإن كان غير مأمون جاز أن يرابط فيه بنفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r11.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r11.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits from Sahl ibn Sa‘d that the Prophet said one day of guarding the frontier is better than the world and all it contains.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#2/r11.anchor: منها ما رواه البخاري عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r1.claim: The Prophet says one day guarding the frontier in God’s path is better with God than the world and everything in it.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r1.anchor: رباط يوم في سبيل الله خير عند الله من الدنيا وما فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r2.speaker: سلمان
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r2.claim: The Prophet says a day and night of ribat surpass a month of fasting and prayer; the reward continues after death, with provision and protection from grave trials.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r2.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن سلمان قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r3.speaker: فضالة بن عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r3.claim: The Prophet says a murabit’s deeds continue to grow until Resurrection and he is protected from the grave’s interrogator, unlike other dead people.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r3.anchor: وروى أبو داود في سننه عن فضالة بن عبيد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r4.claim: These reports show ribat among the best deeds whose reward continues after death, unlike the three ongoing deeds whose effects end when their causes cease.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r4.anchor: وفي هذين الحديثين دليل على أن الرباط أفضل الأعمال التي يبقى ثوابها بعد الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r5.claim: The Prophet names ongoing charity, useful knowledge, and a righteous child’s prayer as the three deeds continuing after a person dies; Muslim alone transmits this sound report.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r5.anchor: كما جاء في حديث العلاء بن عبد الرحمن عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r6.claim: Ribat’s reward multiplies until Resurrection without depending on a cause that later expires, because guarding the faith enables all other acts of worship and Islamic rites.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r6.anchor: والرباط يضاعف أجره إلى يوم القيامة لأنه لا معنى للنماء إلا المضاعفة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r7.claim: A sound Ibn Majah report says dying while guarding the frontier earns the person the continuing reward of his usual good works and protection through Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r7.anchor: من مات مرابطا في سبيل الله أجرى عليه أجر عمله الصالح الذي كان يعمل

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r8.claim: Qurtubi notes that the continuing reward in this report is specifically conditioned on dying while engaged in ribat.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r8.anchor: وفي هذا الحديث قيد ثان وهو الموت حالة الرباط

QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r9.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r9.claim: A report from Uthman attributes to the Prophet that one night of ribat equals a thousand nights of fasting and prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:190-200#3/r9.anchor: وروي عن عثمان بن عفان قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r1.claim: The Madinan surah’s title Āl ʿImrān means the House of ʿImrān, the family line named in verse 33.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r1.anchor: Madinan period, Āl ʿImrān, or “The House ofʿImrān,” refers to the family line

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r2.claim: Early discussion of Quranic interpretation raises the text’s levels of meaning and the spiritual qualities needed to understand it deeply.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r2.anchor: there is a discussion of the interpretation of the Quran (v. 7), raising questions of its levels of meaning

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r3.claim: The surah recounts Mary’s birth and early life, Jesus’s birth and miracles, and his relationship with the apostles.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r3.anchor: the birth and early life of Mary, the mother of Jesus (vv.35–43), the birth of Jesus (vv. 45–47)

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r4.claim: The surah strongly criticizes Jews and Christians among the People of the Book while distinguishing good from bad and affirming some as believers and upright.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r4.anchor: criticizing them strongly, but also distinguishing between the good and the bad among them

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r5.claim: A substantial section addresses the Battle of Uḥud, fought by the believers against the Meccans in 3/625 outside Medina after Badr.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r5.anchor: A considerable portion of this sūrah is devoted to the events of the Battle of Uḥud (3/625)

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r6.claim: The Uhud section addresses cowardice, hypocrisy, worldly attachment, and theological questions including the soul’s state after worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r6.anchor: This part of the sūrah also deals, among other matters, with the moral issues of cowardice, hypocrisy, and worldly attachment

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r7.claim: Some traditions place the revelation of the surah’s first thirty to eighty verses during a visit to Medina by Christians from Najrān.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r7.anchor: It is said that the first part of this chapter (between thirty to eighty verses according to various opinions) was revealed on the occasion

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r8.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r8.claim: One Najrān delegate was said to have been honored by the Byzantines for religious knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r8.anchor: one of whom was said to be honored by the Byzantines for his knowledge of religion (R)

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r9.speaker: Christians
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r9.claim: In the traditional debate, Christians argued Jesus was God because he revived the dead, healed lepers, and spoke of unseen matters.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r9.anchor: they said that Jesus was God, because he revived the dead, healed lepers, and spoke of unseen realities

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r10.speaker: Christians
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r10.claim: They also called Jesus God’s son because he had no human father, and one of three because scripture uses divine first-person plural speech.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r10.anchor: that he was the son of God, because he had no human father; and that he was the third of three

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r11.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r11.claim: The Prophet challenged the sonship claim by asking whether children resemble their fathers and whether Jesus, unlike the living Lord, was subject to death; the Christians agreed.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r11.anchor: Do you not know that our Lord is Living and does not die, and that Jesus is subject to passing away

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r12.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r12.claim: The Prophet asked whether Jesus could sustain, preserve, guard, and provide for all things as God does; the Christians answered no.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r12.anchor: Do you not know that our Lord sustains all things, preserving them, guarding them, providing for them

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r13.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r13.claim: The Prophet argued that nothing is hidden from God and Jesus knew only what he had been taught; the Christians agreed.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r13.anchor: Do you not know that nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from God most high

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r14.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r14.claim: The Prophet contrasted God’s freedom from bodily needs with Jesus’s human birth, feeding, eating, drinking, and bodily functions, asking how the Christian claims could stand.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r14.anchor: God formed Jesus in the womb as He willed, and that our Lord does not eat food, nor consume drink

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r15.claim: The account says the first part of the surah was revealed after the debate with the Christians.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r15.anchor: According to the account, it was after this that the first part of the chapter was revealed (Al, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r16.claim: Āl ʿImrān follows al-Baqarah and is paired with it in virtue reports as the two radiant surahs, al-zahrāwiyān.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r16.anchor: Āl ʿImrān follows al-Baqarah, and in some of the aḥādīth describing the various “virtues” of the Quran it is paired with al-Baqarah

STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r17.claim: A hadith says Quran recitation intercedes for its devotees and the two radiant surahs appear on Judgment Day as clouds, sunrays, or flocks of birds pleading for them.
STUDYQURAN:3:intro/r17.anchor: Recite the Quran, and it will intercede on the Day of Resurrection for those who are devoted to it

BURSEVI:v2p126/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BURSEVI:v2p126/r1.claim: Anas reports that Paradise asks God to admit whoever asks for it three times, and Hell asks God to protect whoever seeks refuge from it three times; the author prays for Paradise and righteous deeds.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r1.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله

BURSEVI:v2p126/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p126/r2.claim: Believers should patiently bear the hardships of obedience and afflictions such as illness, poverty, drought, and fear.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r2.anchor: على مشاق الطاعات وما يصيبكم من الشدائد كالمرض والفقر والقحط والخوف

BURSEVI:v2p126/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p126/r3.claim: They should outlast enemies in the hardships of war and their greatest enemy, the ego, in resisting desire.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r3.anchor: وغالبوا أعداء الله في الصبر على شدائد الحرب وأعدى عدوكم

BURSEVI:v2p126/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p126/r4.claim: Musābara is a particular, harder and better kind of patience, singled out after general patience because of its difficulty and excellence.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r4.anchor: والمصابرة نوع خاص من الصبر ذكر بعد الصبر على ما يجب الصبر عليه تخصيصا لشدته وصعوبته

BURSEVI:v2p126/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p126/r5.claim: Patience progresses from effortful self-restraint, to resisting what blocks it, then sustained commitment, and finally complete patience without strain.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r5.anchor: ثم الاصطبار والاعتبار والالتزام ثم الصبر وهو كماله وحصوله من غير كلفة

BURSEVI:v2p126/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v2p126/r6.claim: The Prophet defines ribāṭ as thorough ablution despite hardship, frequent steps to mosques, and waiting for one prayer after another; these acts erase sins and raise ranks.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r6.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو الله به الخطايا

BURSEVI:v2p126/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p126/r7.claim: Ribāṭ means stationing bodies and horses at frontier posts, and keeping the self on obedience; spiritually, it is vigilance of the innermost self for divine arrivals.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r7.anchor: أبدانكم وخيولكم في النغور مترصدين وأنفسكم على الطاعة

BURSEVI:v2p126/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p126/r8.claim: Taqwā means either disavowing all besides God for complete success or avoiding shameful acts to attain three stations: patience in obedience, resistance to habits, and watchful attention to divine arrivals, corresponding to law, path, and reality.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r8.anchor: واتقوه بالتبرى مما سواه لكي تفلحوا غاية الفلاح أو اتقوا القبائح لعلكم تفلحون

BURSEVI:v2p126/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p126/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p126/r9.claim: The spiritual rank of patience is below musābara, and musābara is below ribāṭ.
BURSEVI:v2p126/r9.anchor: فعلم من هذا أن الصبر دون المصابرة والمصابرة دون المرابطة

QASHANI:3:200/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:200/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:200/r1.claim: Patience for God is struggle at the station of self; mutual patience with God is the heart's encounter with manifestations of majestic attributes.
QASHANI:3:200/r1.anchor: أي: اصبروا في مقام النفس بالمجاهدة، وصابروا في مقام القلب مع سطوات تجليات صفات الجلال بالمكاشفة

QASHANI:3:200/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:200/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:200/r2.claim: Vigilance is the spirit's station: keep the self steady in witnessing, free of lapse, heedlessness, and absence amid changing states.
QASHANI:3:200/r2.anchor: ورابطوا في مقام الروح ذواتكم بالمشاهدة حتى لا يغلبكم فترة أو غفلة أو غيبة بالتلوينات

QASHANI:3:200/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:200/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:200/r3.claim: God-consciousness means avoiding disobedience and display, objection and pride, or lingering selfhood and estrangement at the respective stations, yielding everlasting success.
QASHANI:3:200/r3.anchor: في مقام الصبر عن المخالفة والرياء، وفي المصابرة عن الاعتراض والامتلاء وفي المرابطة عن البقية والجفاء

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r1.claim: God honors patience; the commands mean to be patient, to intensify that patience, and to bind the inward secret to God while standing with Him outwardly.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد : إن الله تعالى ذكر الصبر وشرفه وعظم شأن الصابرين عليه لديه

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r2.claim: True patience is displayed at the first shock of affliction.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r2.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' إنما الصبر عند الصدمة الأولى '

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r3.speaker: الحارث
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r3.claim: Patience means exposing oneself to the arrows of affliction.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r3.anchor: قال الحارث رحمه الله : في قوله تعالى : ﴿ اصبروا ﴾ قال : الصبر : التهدف بسهام البلاء

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r4.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r4.claim: Patience is preparing for trial before it arrives and, when it comes, meeting it through the Lord without despair.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r4.anchor: قال الجريري رحمه الله : الصبر إسبال البلوى قبل وقوع البلوى ، فإذا صادف البلوى تلقاه بالمولى فلم يجزع

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r5.claim: Patience is holding the self with God and refusing despair over anything besides Him.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r5.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : الصبر حبس النفس مع الله تعالى بنفي الجزع عما سواه

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r6.claim: Certainty is the soul's sword and patience a divine secret on earth; Satan fears the patient as believers fear Satan.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : اليقين سيف النفس ، والصبر من سر الله تعالى في أرضه

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r7.speaker: جعفر الخلدي
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r7.claim: A moment of patience brings the best of this world and the next.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r7.anchor: سمعت جعفرا الخلدي رحمه الله يقول : خير الدنيا والآخرة في صبر ساعة

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r8.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r8.claim: The five signs of patience include bearing hardship, remaining dignified despite many dependents, accepting people's abandonment, and speaking truth despite bodily or financial harm.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r8.anchor: قال ذو النون رحمه الله : علامة الصبر خمسة

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r9.claim: Patience accepts God's decree, perseverance faces His enemies in struggle, and steadfastness binds hearts to His approval.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : اصبروا تحت حكمى ، وصابروا في الجهاد مع أعدائي

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r10.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r10.claim: Patience produces contentment, contentment produces modesty, and modesty produces sufficiency.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r10.anchor: وقيل : اصبروا قال : الصبر يوجب الرضا والرضا يوجب الحياء والحياء يوجب الغنى

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r11.speaker: جعفر الصادق
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r11.claim: Be patient in avoiding sins and keeping worship, bind spirits to direct witnessing, and fear God through gracious intimacy with Him to reach the truthful's station.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r11.anchor: قال جعفر الصادق رحمه الله : اصبروا عن المعاصي ، وصابروا على الطاعات

SULAMI:v1p135#4/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r12.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r12.claim: Let bodily limbs endure worship, persevere with God, and bind the inner secrets to realities so that anxieties and passing thoughts fall away.
SULAMI:v1p135#4/r12.anchor: وقال بعضهم : اصبروا بجوارحكم على الطاعات وصابروا مع الله ، ورابطوا أسراركم بالحقائق

SULAMI:v1p137/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p137/r1.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p137/r1.claim: Patience is restraining the self in the face of what it dislikes.
SULAMI:v1p137/r1.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : الصبر حبس النفس على المكروه

TUSTARI:3:200/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:200/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:200/r1.claim: Faith rests on four pillars: reliance on God, surrender to His command, acceptance of His decree, and gratitude for His blessings, together with piety.
TUSTARI:3:200/r1.anchor: قال: الإيمان أربعة أركان: الأول التوكل على الله، والثاني الاستسلام لأمره

TUSTARI:3:200/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:200/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:200/r2.claim: Certainty is faith's heart, patience its support, and sincerity its completion; certainty's inner witnessing produces sincerity, which leads through affirmation and realization to the Real.
TUSTARI:3:200/r2.anchor: اليقين قلب الإيمان، والصبر عماد الإيمان، والإخلاص كمال الإيمان

FARRA:v1p250/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p250/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p250/r7.claim: Believers should endure with their Prophet in jihad and outlast their enemy in patience.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r1.claim: صابروا means persist against your enemy.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r2.claim: رباط originally meant opposing forces tying and preparing their horses at a frontier; residence at the frontier consequently came to be called ribāṭ.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r2.anchor: أن يربط هؤلاء خيولهم، ويربط هؤلاء خيولهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p117#6/r3.claim: تفلحون means winning enduring, everlasting life; falāḥ originally means remaining.

MAJAZ:v1p112/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p112/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p112/r2.claim: رابطوا means stand firm and persist.

MAJAZ:v1p112/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p112/r3.speaker: الأخطل
MAJAZ:v1p112/r3.claim: Al-Akhṭal's poem uses ribāṭ for horses stationed and prepared, and for enduring shame among Banū Kulayb.
MAJAZ:v1p112/r3.anchor: قال الأخطل: ما زال فينا رباط الخيل معلمة

NAHHAS:v1p429/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p429/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p429/r1.claim: اصبروا is an imperative, so its plural nūn is dropped.

NAHHAS:v1p429/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p429/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p429/r2.claim: وصابروا, رابطوا, and اتقوا are coordinated; taqwa should govern all affairs, not only jihad.
NAHHAS:v1p429/r2.anchor: وصابروا ورابطوا ) عطف عليه وكذا ( واتقوا الله ) أي لا يكن وكدكم الجهاد فقط

NAHHAS:v1p429/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p429/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p429/r3.claim: لعلكم تفلحون expresses hope of success; al-Dahhak explains falah as remaining or enduring.
NAHHAS:v1p429/r3.anchor: لعلكم تفلحون ) أي لتكونوا على رجاء من الفلاح قال الضحاك الفلاح البقاء

IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي : انه كان يقول في هذه الاية : اصبروا وصابروا يقول : اصبروا على دينكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r2.claim: Remain steadfast in Islam, God’s chosen religion, through ease, hardship, and every condition until death.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r2.anchor: قال الحسن : امروا ان يصبروا على دينهم الذي ارتضاه الله لهم لاسلام ، فلا ندعوا لسراء ولا لضراء

IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r3.claim: Be patient in fulfilling the religious obligations; Muqatil ibn Hayyan reports similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله تعالى : يا ايها الذين امنوا اصبروا يعني : على الفرائض

IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r4.speaker: أبو غسان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r4.claim: The verse was revealed about remaining in the mosques.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي غسان قال : ان هذه الاية انما نزلت في لزوم المساجد

IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r5.claim: Be patient in maintaining the prayers.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r5.anchor: عن الحسن : اصبروا وصابروا قال : اصبروا على الصلوات

IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r6.claim: Be patient in jihad; Muhammad ibn Kaʿb also explains it as patience against the enemy.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r6.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : اصبروا : على الجهاد - وروي عن محمد بن كعب قول اخر لانه قال : اصبروا وصابروا : للعدو

IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r7.claim: Be patient in fulfilling God’s rights.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : يا ايها الذين امنوا اصبروا وصابروا قال : اصبروا على حق الله

IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p847#2/r8.anchor: عن الحسن قوله : اصبروا وصابروا قال : اصبروا على المصائب

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r1.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : اصبروا وصابروا قال : اصبروا على الخير

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r2.claim: Persevere until the promise made to you is fulfilled.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي ؛ انه كان يقول في هذه الاية : اصبروا وصابروا يقول : صابروا الوعد الذي وعدتكم عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r3.claim: Withstand the unbelievers until they tire of their religion; Zayd ibn Aslam, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Qatada report comparable explanations.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r3.anchor: سمعت الحسن ، وقرا هذه الاية : اصبروا وصابروا قال : امروا ان يصبروا عن الكفار ، حتى يكون في الكفار الذين يملون دينهم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r4.claim: Vie with your enemy in patience.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r4.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم انه قال : صابروا عدوكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r5.claim: Stand firm with the Prophet in the field of battle.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله تعالى : يا ايها الذين امنوا اصبروا وصابروا يعني : مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الموطن

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r6.anchor: عن الحسن قال : سمعته يقول في قوله : اصبروا وصابروا على الصلوات

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says to persevere in your religion.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r7.anchor:
سالت الحسن عن قوله : اصبروا وصابروا 
قال : صابروا على دينكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r8.claim: Persevere against the adherents of error.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r8.anchor: عن قتادة : اصبروا وصابروا قال : صابروا اهل الضلالة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r9.speaker: النبي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r9.claim: The Prophet said that thorough ablution despite hardship, walking often to mosques, and waiting for each prayer after the next erase sins and raise ranks; he called this ribat three times.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p848/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : الا اخبركم بما يمحوا الله به الخطايا ، ويرفع به الدرجات

IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r1.claim: Guard against God’s enemy and your enemy until he abandons his religion for yours; al-Hasan and Qatada similarly interpret the command as posting against polytheists.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r1.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي ؛ انه كان يقول في هذه الاية : ورابطوا يقول : رابطوا عدوي وعدوكم حتى يترك دينه لدينكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r2.claim: Remain steadfast in what God commanded and forbade.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : ورابطوا يعني : فيما امركم ونهاكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r3.claim: Remain steadfast in your religion; al-Hasan reports the same.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r3.anchor: عن زيد بن اسلم في قوله : ورابطوا قال : رابطوا على دينكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r4.claim: Keep watch against the enemy alongside the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r4.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : ورابطوا : مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم العدو

IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r5.claim: Ribat also refers to the person who remains seated after prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r5.anchor: عن عبد الحميد بن عمران ، حدثنا بشير بن أبي سلمة ؛ انه سمع محمد بن كعب يقول : ورابطوا قال : الذي يقعد بعد الصلاة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r6.claim: Fear God in what lies between Him and you.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r6.anchor: محمد بن كعب يقول : ورابطوا قال : الذي يقعد بعد الصلاة .

IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r7.claim: Qatada recites the full command to be patient, persevere, guard, and fear God, without an added gloss in this report.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r7.anchor: عن قتادة اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون

IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r8.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r8.claim: They may prosper tomorrow when they meet God; this is the promised outcome of patience and perseverance.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p850/r8.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي انه كان يقول في هذه الاية اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون يقول : لعلكم تفلحون غدا اذا لقيتموني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.claim: The surah closes by renewing believers’ resolve and readiness against the enemy so the defeat they suffered will not demoralize them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r1.anchor: ختمت السورة بوصاية جامعة للمؤمنين تجدد عزيمتهم وتبعث الهمم إلى دوام الاستعداد للعدو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r2.claim: Patience gathers the virtues; mutual perseverance means holding firm against another patient opponent, a harder and more precarious trial because the rival may equal or surpass one.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.claim: A contest is won by whoever endures longer; if one yields before the other tires, one gains nothing from patience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r3.anchor: لأن نتيجة الصبر تكون لأطول الصابرين صبرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.speaker: زفر بن الحارث
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.claim: Zufar ibn al-Ḥārith’s verse excuses a retreat by saying both sides drank the same cup, but the enemy proved more patient in facing death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r4.anchor: كما قال زفر بن الحارث في اعتذاره عن الانهزام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.speaker: شاعر العرب الذي لم يعرف اسمه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.claim: An unnamed Arab poet says perseverance in battle brings fire upon one’s enemies, illustrating the author’s claim that mutual endurance wins war.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p207#2/r5.anchor: كما قال شاعر العرب الذي لم يعرف اسمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r1.claim: Ribāṭ means keeping horses tethered for watch at vulnerable approaches beyond active fighting, so Muslims remain alert to surprise attacks after Uḥud; the Confederates later attacked in just such circumstances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r1.anchor: وهي مفاعلة من الربط ، وهو ربط الخيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r2.claim: Ribāṭ was already a pre-Islamic practice of guarding tribal approaches and mountain passes; after Islamic expansion it included land and coastal frontier stations vulnerable to enemy landings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r2.anchor: وكانت المرابطة معروفة في الجاهلية وهي ربط الفرس للحراسة في الثغور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r3.speaker: لبيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r3.claim: Labīd’s poem vividly depicts a mounted guard watching the tribal settlement from a high lookout until darkness covers the vulnerable passes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r3.anchor: وما رأيت من وصف ذلك مثل لبيد في معلقته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r4.claim: God commands frontier guard just as He commands fighting, in the established sense of maintaining watch at land and sea approaches.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r4.anchor: فأمر الله بالرباط كما أمر بالجهاد بهذا المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r5.claim: Some commentators instead take ribāṭ as preparing horses tethered for battle and argue there were no frontier campaigns in the Prophet’s time; the author says this misses the established meaning.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r6.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r6.claim: Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is associated with interpreting ribāṭ as waiting for one prayer after another, based on Abū Hurayra’s report in Mālik’s Muwaṭṭaʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r6.anchor: ونسب هذا لأبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r7.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet described waiting for the next prayer after one as ribāṭ, repeating the phrase three times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r7.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r8.claim: The author says prayer-waiting is metaphorical, like the reports that strength is not merely wrestling and poverty is not merely asking for food; he also invokes the saying about returning from lesser to greater struggle as figurative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p208/r8.anchor: والحق أن معنى هذا الحديث على التشبيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r1.claim: The surah closes with a charge combining worldly victory over enemies and the afterlife’s bliss: be patient in obedience and against desires.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r1.anchor: ختم الله تعالى السورة بهذه الوصاة التي جمعت الظهور في الدنيا على الأعداء، والفوز بنعيم الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets muṣābara as steadfastness against the enemy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r2.anchor: بالمصابرة فقيل: معناه مصابرة الأعداء، قاله زيد بن أسلم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi takes it as patient confidence in God’s promise of victory: do not tire, but await relief; a saying about waiting patiently for relief is attributed to the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه: مصابرة وعد الله في النصر، قاله محمد بن كعب القرظي: أي لا تسأموا وانتظروا الفرج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r4.speaker: جمهور الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r4.claim: The majority understand ribāṭ as tying and keeping horses ready as enemies do, linked to the command about cavalry readiness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r4.anchor:
فقال جمهور الأمة معناه: رابطوا أعداءكم الخيل، أي ارتبطوها كما
يرتبطها أعداؤكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r5.claim: In a letter to Abu ʿUbayda about Roman forces, ʿUmar says hardship for a believer is followed by relief and cites this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r5.anchor: وكتب عمر بن الخطاب إلى أبي عبيدة، وقد كتب إليه يذكر جموع الروم، فكتب إليه عمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r6.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r6.claim: Abu Salama says the verse is about waiting for each prayer after the previous one, since there was no frontier fighting to guard in the Prophet’s time.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r6.anchor: وقد قال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: هذه الآية هي في انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو هريرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r7.claim: A report from these Companions says ritual washing through hardship, walking often to mosques, and awaiting the next prayer erase sins and raise ranks; it calls this ribāṭ three times.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r7.anchor: واحتج بحديث علي بن أبي طالب وجابر بن عبد الله وأبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ألا أدلكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r8.claim: The original lexical sense is holding the frontier for God, from tying horses; the prayer-waiting report uses ribāṭ by analogy because prayer is a saving path.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r8.anchor: والقول الصحيح هو أن الرباط هو الملازمة في سبيل الله أصلها من ربط الخيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r9.speaker: ابن المواز
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r9.claim: Jurists define a murābiṭ as someone who travels to a frontier and remains there for a period; permanent residents working there with their families are not technically murābiṭūn, though they protect it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r9.anchor: والمرابط في سبيل الله عند الفقهاء: هو الذي يشخص إلى ثغر من الثغور ليرابط فيه مدة ما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r10.claim: Laʿallakum tufliḥūn expresses hope from the human point of view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p559#3/r10.anchor: وقوله: لعلكم تفلحون ترج في حق البشر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r1.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r1.claim: Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman says the verse was revealed about waiting for one prayer after another, at a time without a campaign requiring frontier watch.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة وليس يؤمئذ غزو يرابط

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r2.claim: Patience is variously explained as enduring trials and jihad (Ibn ʿAbbas), religion (al-Hasan, al-Qurazi, al-Zajjaj), afflictions (al-Hasan), obligations (Saʿid ibn Jubayr), or obedience to God (Qatada).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r2.anchor: البلاء والجهاد قاله ابن عباس الثاني الدين قاله الحسن والقرظي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r3.claim: The command to outlast others is explained as steadfastness against the enemy by Ibn ʿAbbas and most authorities, or steadfastness in God’s promise by ʿAta and al-Qurazi.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r3.anchor: العدو قاله ابن عباس والجمهور والثاني الوعد الذي وعدهم الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r4.claim: Frontier ribat means preparing horses against the enemy, with each side readying its horses, as Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Qatada, and others say.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r4.anchor: الجهاد للأعداء قاله ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r5.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r5.claim: Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman gives an alternative: maintaining vigilance in prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p533#2/r5.anchor: أنه الصلاة أمروا بالمرابطة عليها قاله أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says believers must remain steadfast in Islam through ease and hardship until death, and persevere against enemies who conceal their religion; other early scholars agree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r3.anchor: قال الحسن البصري، رحمه الله: أمروا أن يصبروا على دينهم الذي ارتضاه الله لهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r4.claim: Ribat can mean persisting and remaining firm in a place of worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r4.anchor: وأما المرابطة فهي المداومة في مكان العبادة والثبات.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r5.claim: Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, Sahl ibn Hunayf, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others explain ribat as waiting for one prayer after another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة، قاله [مجاهد و] (11) ابن عباس وسهل بن حنيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that completing ablution despite difficulty, walking often to mosques, and waiting between prayers erase sins and raise ranks; these acts are called ribat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r6.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ألا أخبركم بما يمحو الله به الخطايا، ويرفع به الدرجات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra says the verse addressed people who maintained mosque prayers on time and remembered God there: endure the five prayers, resist the self and desires, and remain in mosques.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p195#2/r7.anchor: أقبل علي أبو هريرة يوما فقال: أتدري يا ابن أخي فيم نزلت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r1.claim: Al-Hakim transmits a route corroborating Abu Hurayra's report that the verse's ribat was waiting between prayers because there was no wartime frontier post in the Prophet's era.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r1.anchor: عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي هريرة -بنحوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r2.claim: Ali reports the Prophet's teaching that thorough ablution in difficulty and waiting from prayer to prayer expiate sins; this is ribat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r2.anchor: عن شرحبيل، عن علي، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا أدلكم على ما يكفر الذنوب والخطايا؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r3.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet listing thorough ablution, many steps to mosques, and waiting between prayers as expiation of sins and ribat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r3.anchor: عن شرحبيل، عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو الله به الخطايا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r4.claim: Abu Ayyub reports the Prophet identifying ablution, frequent mosque walks, and waiting between prayers as ribat in mosques, explicitly linking them to this verse; Ibn Kathir calls this route very unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r4.anchor: قال: "وهو قول الله تعالى: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون} فذلك هو الرباط في المساجد"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r5.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r5.claim: Abu Salama says the verse did not concern military frontier posts in the Prophet's time but waiting from one prayer to the next; Ibn Kathir notes the earlier version is Abu Hurayra's wording, God knows best.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p196/r5.anchor: قال لي أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: يا ابن أخي، هل تدري في أي شيء نزلت هذه الآية {اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r1.claim: Another interpretation is military ribat: guarding Islam's frontiers against enemy entry, for which reports promise abundant reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r1.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالمرابطة هاهنا مرابطة الغزو في نحور العدو، وحفظ ثغور الإسلام وصيانتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r2.claim: Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi reports the Prophet saying one day stationed in God's cause is better than the world and everything in it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r2.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي، رضي الله عنه (3) أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "رباط يوم في سبيل الله خير من الدنيا وما عليها"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r3.claim: Salman reports that a day and night of ribat surpass a month of fasting and prayer; if the guard dies there, his deeds and provision continue and he is safe from the testers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r3.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي، عن رسوله الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "رباط يوم وليلة خير من صيام شهر وقيامه، وإن مات جرى عليه عمله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r4.claim: Fadala ibn Ubayd reports that a martyr's deeds cease except for one who dies guarding the frontier, whose deeds grow until resurrection and who is spared the grave trial; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r4.anchor: أنه سمع فضالة بن عبيد يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "كل ميت يختم على عمله، إلا الذي مات مرابطا في سبيل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r5.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Lahi'a's explicit transmission is acceptable, especially when supported by the preceding corroborating reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r5.anchor: وابن لهيعة إذا صرح بالتحديث فهو حسن، ولا سيما مع ما تقدم من الشواهد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r6.claim: Uqba ibn Amir reports that a frontier guard's deeds continue until resurrection and he is protected from the testers; Ibn Mardawayh also transmits a shorter version omitting that protection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p197/r6.anchor: سمعت عقبة بن عامر يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "كل ميت يختم له على عمله، إلا المرابط في سبيل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that one dying in ribat keeps receiving his righteous deeds and provision, is safe from the testers, and rises secure from the great terror.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من مات مرابطا في سبيل الله، أجري (7) عليه عمله الصالح الذي كان يعمل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r2.claim: Another Abu Hurayra report says the deceased guard is protected from the grave trial and greatest terror, receives Paradise's provision morning and evening, and earns ribat's reward until resurrection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من مات مرابطا وقي فتنة القبر، وأمن (9) من الفزع الأكبر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r3.speaker: أم الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r3.claim: Umm al-Darda raises a report that three days guarding any Muslim coastline suffice as a year of ribat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r3.anchor: عن أم الدرداء ترفع الحديث قالت (11) من رابط في شيء من سواحل المسلمين ثلاثة أيام، أجزأت عنه رباط سنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r4.speaker: عثمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r4.claim: Uthman reports from the Prophet that one night guarding in God's cause is better than a thousand nights spent in prayer and fasting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r4.anchor: قال عثمان، رضي الله عنه -وهو يخطب على منبره-: إني محدثكم حديثا سمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r5.speaker: عثمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r5.claim: A second Uthman transmission says one night of ribat equals a thousand nights of fasting and standing in worship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p198/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال: خطب عثمان بن عفان الناس فقال: يأيها الناس، إني سمعت حديثا من رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r1.speaker: عثمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r1.claim: Uthman reports that one day of ribat in God's cause is better than a thousand days elsewhere; al-Tirmidhi grades this route hasan gharib.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح مولى عثمان بن عفان قال: سمعت عثمان -وهو على المنبر-يقول: إني كتمتكم حديثا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r2.speaker: عثمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r2.claim: Ahmad's version adds Uthman's invitation to choose whether to serve at the frontier, followed by his asking God to witness that he conveyed the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r2.anchor: فقال -يعني عثمان-: فليرابط امرؤ كيف شاء، هل بلغت؟ قالوا: نعم. قال: اللهم اشهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r3.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r3.claim: Salman tells Shurahbil that one day of ribat exceeds a month of fasting and prayer, and that death there brings protection from the grave trial and continuing deeds; al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r3.anchor: مر سلمان الفارسي بشرحبيل بن السمط، وهو في مرابط له، وقد شق عليه وعلى أصحابه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r4.claim: Although some copies say Ibn al-Munkadir's chain from Salman is disconnected, Ibn Kathir thinks he heard it from Shurahbil; Muslim and al-Nasa'i transmit corroborating routes through Shurahbil, Salman, and the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199/r4.anchor: وفي بعض النسخ زيادة: وليس إسناده بمتصل، وابن المنكدر لم يدرك سلمان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b's report promises immense reward for guarding a Muslim vulnerable frontier: a day outside Ramadan equals a hundred years of worship and a Ramadan day a thousand; the returning guard remains sinless and earns ribat reward until Judgment. Ibn Kathir calls this route gharib and munkar, and its transmitter Umar ibn Subayh accused.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r1.anchor: عن مكحول، عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لرباط يوم في سبيل الله، من وراء عورة المسلمين محتسبا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.claim: Anas reports one night of guarding surpasses a man's thousand years of fasting and worship at home, counting a year as 360 days; Ibn Kathir calls it gharib and notes Sa'id ibn Khalid was weakened and accused of unsupported and fabricated reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن خالد بن أبي طويل، سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "حرس ليلة في سبيل الله أفضل من صيام رجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.claim: A report asks God to show mercy to the sentry; Ibn Kathir notes a broken link because Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz did not meet Uqba ibn Amir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p199#2/r3.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز، عن عقبة بن عامر الجهني قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "رحم الله حارس الحرس"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p200/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p200/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p200/r1.claim: At Hunayn, Anas ibn Abi Mirthad volunteers to guard a mountain pass overnight after a scout reports Hawazin assembled there; he returns by morning and the Prophet says his service has earned its reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p200/r1.anchor: حدثه سهل ابن الحنظلية (7) أنهم ساروا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم حنين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p200/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p200/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p200/r2.claim: On a cold campaign night, Abu Rayhana recounts the Prophet praying extensively for an Ansari volunteer who guarded, then more briefly for Abu Rayhana; the Prophet says fire is forbidden to an eye weeping from God's fear or kept awake in God's cause.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p200/r2.anchor: سمعت أبا ريحانة يقول: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r1.claim: Al-Nasa'i transmits Abu Rayhana's report that fire is forbidden to eyes that weep from fear of God or keep vigil in God's cause, through routes naming Abu Ali al-Janbi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r1.anchor: وروى النسائي منه: "حرمت النار ... " إلى آخره عن عصمة بن الفضل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that two eyes will not be touched by fire: one weeping in fear of God and one keeping watch in God's cause; al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan gharib and says it is known only through Shu'ayb ibn Ruzayq.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "عينان لا تمسهما النار: عين بكت من خشية الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r3.claim: Mu'adh ibn Anas reports that a volunteer who guards Muslims without a ruler's wage will not see the Fire except for the passage required by the oath; Ahmad alone transmits it, and it cites the universal passage over Hell.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r3.anchor: عن أبيه معاذ بن أنس، رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من حرس من وراء المسلمين في سبيل الله متطوعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra's report contrasts the resentful servant of money and fine clothes with the rough, dusty horseman in God's cause, content to guard or serve in the rear and without status.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " تعس عبد الدينار وعبد الدرهم وعبد الخميصة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r5.claim: In a letter encouraging Abu Ubayda amid Roman forces, Umar says hardship for a believer is followed by relief and cites this verse, adding that one hardship will not overcome two eases.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p201/r5.anchor: فكتب إليه عمر: أما بعد فإنه مهما ينزل بعبد مؤمن من منزلة شدة يجعل الله بعدها فرجا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p202/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p202/r1.speaker: ابن المبارك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p202/r1.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak's Tarsus poem to al-Fudayl contrasts worship in the holy sanctuaries with frontier service: fighters shed blood, endure dust and heat, and cite the Prophet and Qur'an for the martyr's merit; al-Fudayl weeps and calls it sincere counsel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p202/r1.anchor: قال: أملى علي عبد الله بن المبارك هذه الأبيات بطرسوس، وودعته للخروج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p202/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p202/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p202/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a man unable to sustain uninterrupted prayer and fasting asks how to earn fighters' reward; the Prophet says he could not match them and even a campaigning horse earns good deeds while exercising at its tether.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p202/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله علمني عملا أنال به ثواب المجاهدين في سبيل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r1.claim: God-consciousness is required in every affair and circumstance; the Prophet advised Mu'adh to fear God everywhere, follow a bad deed with a good one, and treat people well.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r1.anchor: وقوله: {واتقوا الله} أي: في جميع أموركم وأحوالكم، كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاذ [بن جبل]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r2.claim: The promise of flourishing means success in this life and the next.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b glosses the command as fearing God in what lies between Him and people, so they may succeed when they meet Him tomorrow.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p203/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي: أنه كان يقول في قول الله عز وجل: {واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون} واتقوا الله فيما بيني وبينكم

JISHUMI:v2p1439/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r1.claim: Ribāṭ and murābaṭa share a root sense of tying; military ribāṭ means remaining at a frontier to repel enemy harm, like tethering horses, while muṣābara is mutual steadfastness.
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r1.anchor: الرباط والمرابطة واحد، وأصل الربط الشد، ربطت الشيء أربطه ربطا

JISHUMI:v2p1439/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r2.claim: The commands follow the account of believers and unbelievers to urge obedience, religious commitment, and jihad; alternatively believers should emulate those who fought and died and their reward.
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r2.anchor: لما حكى تعالى أحوال المؤمنين والكافرين فيما تقدم حث على الصبر على الطاعة

JISHUMI:v2p1439/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن جريج والضحاك
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r3.claim: They interpret the sequence as patience in obeying God, steadfastness against God's enemies in jihad, and guarding the frontier for God's cause.
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r3.anchor: اصبروا على طاعة الله وصابروا أعداء الله في الجهاد ورابطوا في سبيل الله عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v2p1439/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r4.claim: He interprets it as steadfastness in religion, mutual competition in response to God's promises, and standing against enemies.
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r4.anchor: اصبروا على دينكم، وصابروا وعدي إياكم، ورابطوا أعداءكم عن محمد بن كعب

JISHUMI:v2p1439/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r5.claim: He reads the commands as patience in jihad, endurance against the enemy, and tethering horses for battle.
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r5.anchor: اصبروا على الجهاد، وصابروا العدو، ورابطوا الخيل عليه عن زيد بن أسلم

JISHUMI:v2p1439/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r6.claim: He interprets ribāṭ as waiting for one prayer after another.
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r6.anchor: ورابطوا بانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v2p1439/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r7.claim: Success may mean attaining the desired reward, avoiding the nullification of good deeds, or doing these acts in hope of success.
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r7.anchor: لعلكم تفلحون يعني لتفلحوا؛ أي لتنالوا البغية من الثواب

JISHUMI:v2p1439/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r8.claim: The commands cover duty: worship and avoiding sin, opposing adversaries by hand and tongue, defending Islam at frontiers, and avoiding all wrongdoing; success depends on such acts, against the Murjiʾa.
JISHUMI:v2p1439/r8.anchor: تدل الآية على جماع ما يتناوله التكليف؛ لأن قوله: اصبروا يتناول العبادات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r1.claim: Be steadfast in religion and obligations; outlast God’s enemies in jihad by enduring hardship, this specialized patience being singled out after patience generally.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r1.anchor: اصبروا على الدين وتكاليفه ﴿ وصابروا ﴾ أعداء الله في الجهاد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r2.claim: Ribāṭ means staying at frontier posts with horses ready for a raid, as in 8:60.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r2.anchor: وأقيموا في الثغور رابطين خيلكم فيها مترصدين مستعدين للغزو قال الله عز وجل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r3.claim: A Prophetic report equates a day and night guarding the frontier with a month of fasting and prayer, uninterrupted except for need.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r3.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 247 ( من رابط يوما وليلة في سبيل الله كان كعدل صيام شهر وقيامه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r4.claim: A report promises safety on the bridge over Hell for every verse of Āl ʿImrān to its reciter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r4.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم 248 ( من قرأ سورة آل عمران أعطى بكل آية منها امانا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r5.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r5.claim: Another report says God and His angels bless whoever recites Āl ʿImrān on Friday until sunset.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p488#2/r5.anchor: وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام 249 ( من قرأ السورة التي يذكر فيها آل عمران يوم الجمعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن جريج والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r3.claim: The commands mean be patient in obeying God, endure against His enemies, and guard the frontier in His cause.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r3.anchor: اصبروا على طاعة الله , وصابروا أعداء الله , ورابطوا في سبيل الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r4.claim: The commands mean remain steadfast in your religion, persist in expectation of God's promise, and watch for His and your enemy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r4.anchor: اصبروا على دينكم , وصابروا الوعد الذي وعدكم , ورابطوا عدوي وعدوكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r5.claim: The commands mean persevere in jihad, confront the enemy, and stay stationed at the frontier; ribāṭ derives from binding oneself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r5.anchor: اصبروا على الجهاد , وصابروا العدو , ورابطوا بملازمة الثغر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet teaching that thorough ablution despite hardship, many steps to mosques, and waiting from one prayer to the next erase sins and raise ranks; this is ribāṭ.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p444#2/r6.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ألا أدلكم على ما يحط به الله الخطايا ويرفع به الدرجات

MUJAHID:v1p141#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p141#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v1p141#2/r1.claim: Be patient in remaining steadfast in your religion; contend with unbelievers until they tire of their religion; and stand guard against the polytheists.
MUJAHID:v1p141#2/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا ﴾ فيقول اصبروا على دينكم ﴿ وصابروا ﴾ الكفار حتى يملوا دينهم ﴿ ورابطوا ﴾ المشركين

MUQATIL:3:200/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:200/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:200/r1.claim: Believers must obey God’s commands and obligations, stand firm alongside the Prophet in campaigns, guard against the enemy until it abandons its religion for theirs, and avoid disobedience to attain success.
MUQATIL:3:200/r1.anchor: على أمر الله عز وجل وفرائضه، { وصابروا } مع النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:3:200/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:200/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MUQATIL:3:200/r2.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas quotes the Prophet’s pact with Najran: tribute in garments, protection for people, property, and Christian institutions, and provisions on loans, taxes, and justice.
MUQATIL:3:200/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، رضى الله عنه، قال: كتب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأهل نجران:

MUQATIL:3:200#2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r1.claim: The pact lists Abu Sufyan b. Harb, Ghaylan b. ʿAmr, Malik b. ʿAwf, al-Aqraʿ b. Habis, and al-Mughira as witnesses; the account says Abu Bakr copied a document from the Prophet’s original.
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r1.anchor: شهد أبو سفيان بن حرب، وغيلان بن عمرو، ومالك بن عوف النضرى، والأقرع ابن حابس،

MUQATIL:3:200#2/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r2.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r2.claim: In a report about Najran, ʿAli refused to criticize ʿUmar, telling the delegation that ʿUmar had acted wisely.
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r2.anchor: عن سالم بن أبى الجعد، قال: لو كان عليا طاعنا على عمر بن الخطاب،

MUQATIL:3:200#2/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r3.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r3.claim: Salem’s account says Najran’s population grew to forty thousand fighters, conflict arose, and ʿUmar refused a request to return after their reconciliation, sending groups to Syria, Iraq, and elsewhere.
MUQATIL:3:200#2/r3.anchor: قال: كثروا حتى صاروا أربعين ألف مقاتل، فخاف المسلمون أن يميلوا عليهم،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r1.claim: Believers must be patient in religion and its duties.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r1.anchor: على الدين وتكاليفه قال الجنيد رضى الله عنه الصبر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r2.speaker: الجنيد
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r2.claim: Al-Junayd defines patience as restraining oneself from what is disliked without agitation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد رضى الله عنه الصبر حبس النفس على المكروه بنفى الجزع

NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r3.claim: Compete with God's enemies in jihad by enduring war's hardships, showing no less patience or steadfastness than they do.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r3.anchor: أعداء الله فى الجهاد أى غالبوهم فى الصبر على شدائد الحرب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r4.claim: Maintain posts at the frontier, keeping horses there while watchful and ready to fight.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r4.anchor: وأقيموا فى الثغور رابطين خيلكم فيها مترصدين مستعدين للغزو

NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r5.claim: Falah is remaining with what one loves after escaping hardship; laʿalla keeps the outcome uncertain so believers do not rely on hopes without doing good first.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r5.anchor: الفلاح البقاء مع المحبوب بعد الخلاص عن المكروه ولعل لتغيب المآل لئلا يتكلوا على الآمال عن تقديم الأعمال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r6.claim: A spiritual interpretation reads the commands as patience in God's love, perseverance amid His favors, and tethering the self in His service to attain closeness.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r6.anchor: وقيل اصبروا فى محبتى وصابروا فى نعمتى ورابطوا أنفسكم فى خدمتى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r7.claim: The Prophet says the two radiant chapters, al-Baqara and Āl ʿImrān, will come on Judgment Day as clouds or flocks of birds, pleading for their companions.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p201/r7.anchor: قال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرؤوا الزهراوين البقرة وسورة آل عمران فانهما يأتيان يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r4.claim: The closing verse gathers ten exhortations and promises worldly victory over enemies and success in the afterlife; patience is required in obedience and against desires.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r4.anchor: ختم تعالى السورة بما تضمنته هذه الآية العاشرة من الوصاة التي جمعت الظهور في الدنيا على الأعداء والفوز بنعيم الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam interprets sabiru as steadfastness against enemies.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r5.anchor: معناه مصابرة الأعداء قاله زيد بن أسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r6.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r6.claim: Al-Hasan interprets sabiru as persevering in the five daily prayers.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r7.speaker: عطاء والقرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r7.claim: Ata and al-Qurazi interpret sabiru as patiently awaiting God's promised relief without despair; Abu Umar chooses this view, though the enemy-facing interpretation is the majority view.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r7.anchor: وقال عطاء والقرظي: صابروا الوعد الذي وعدتم. أي لا تيأسوا وانتظروا الفرج

QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r8.claim: A report says waiting patiently for relief is an act of worship.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r9.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r9.claim: Antara's verse illustrates sabiru as standing firm against an enemy in battle without cowardice; mukafaha denotes facing and confronting in combat.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r9.anchor:
فلم أر حيا صابروا مثل صبرنا
ولا كافحوا مثل الذين نكافح

QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r10.speaker: جمهور الأمة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r10.claim: The majority interpret rabitu as stationing and tethering horses to face the enemy, as the Quran elsewhere mentions tethered war-horses.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r10.anchor: فقال جمهور الأمة: رابطوا أعداءكم بالخيل، أي ارتبطواها كما يرتبطها أعداءكم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r11.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r11.claim: In a letter to Abu Ubayda about Roman forces, Umar says hardship is followed by relief, one hardship will not defeat two eases, and cites this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:199-200/r11.anchor: كتب أبو عبيدة بن الجراح إلى عمر بن الخطاب يذكر له جموعا من الروم وما يتخوف منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b reports that a day of ribat outside Ramadan earns more than a century of fasting and prayer; during Ramadan it earns more than a millennium, and the reward continues after safe return.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r1.anchor: لرباط يوم في سبيل الله من وراء عورة المسلمين محتسبا من غير شهر رمضان أعظم أجرا من عبادة مائة سنة
