QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi infers that a day of Ramadan ribat brings enduring reward even if the person returns safely rather than dying on duty.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r2.anchor: ودل هذا الحديث على أن رباط يوم في شهر رمضان يحصل له من الثواب الدائم وإن لم يمت مرابطا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r3.claim: Anas reports that one night guarding in God's path exceeds a thousand years of fasting and night prayer at home, with each year counted as 360 days and each day as a thousand years.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r3.anchor: حرس ليلة في سبيل الله أفضل من صيام رجل وقيامه في أهله ألف سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r4.claim: Because waiting for one prayer after another is also called ribat, those waiting for prayers may receive this merit, God willing.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r4.anchor: وجاء في انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة أنه رباط فقد يحصل لمنتظر الصلوات ذلك الفضل

QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r5.claim: The Prophet praised Muslims who completed Maghrib and awaited Isha, saying God opened heaven and boasted of them to the angels.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r6.claim: Taqwa means the believers were not commanded to fight without piety; la'allakum may express hope or purpose, and falah means enduring success, points discussed fully in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:200/r6.anchor: واتقوا الله } أي لم تؤمروا بالجهاد من غير تقوى. { لعلكم تفلحون } لتكونوا على رجاء من الفلاح

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r1.claim: The surah’s closing verse gathers its teachings: the foundations of faith include monotheism, divine justice, prophethood, and resurrection, while its practical rulings include pilgrimage and jihad.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r1.anchor: أنواعا كثيرة من علوم الأصول والفروع

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r2.claim: Human circumstances are individual or shared: patience applies to what concerns oneself, while steadfastly bearing what occurs with others is muṣābara.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r2.anchor: منها ما يتعلق به وحده ، ومنها ما يكون مشتركا بينه وبين غيره

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r3.claim: Patience includes bearing the intellectual work of proving monotheism, justice, prophethood, and resurrection and answering opponents’ doubts.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r3.anchor: أن يصبر على مشقة النظر والاستدلال في معرفة التوحيد والعدل والنبوة والمعاد

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r4.claim: Patience also means enduring the difficulty of performing obligatory and recommended acts.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r4.anchor: أن يصبر على مشقة أداء الواجبات والمندوبات

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r5.claim: Patience includes bearing the difficulty of avoiding prohibited acts.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r5.anchor: أن يصبر على مشقة الاحتراز عن المنهيات

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r6.claim: It also covers worldly trials and afflictions, including illness, poverty, drought, and fear.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r6.anchor: الصبر على شدائد الدنيا وآفاتها من المرض والفقر والقحط والخوف

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r7.claim: Muṣābara includes enduring bad conduct by family, neighbors, and relatives, and refraining from retaliation; the author cites 7:199 and 25:72.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r7.anchor: ويدخل فيه تحمل الاخلاق الردية من أهل البيت والجيران والأقارب

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r8.claim: It includes preferring others over oneself, linked to 59:9.

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r9.claim: It includes forgiving someone who wronged you, since forgiving is nearer to God-consciousness (2:237).

RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r10.claim: It includes enjoining right and forbidding wrong, jihad despite exposure to harm, and persevering with opponents while resolving their doubts and removing falsehood from their hearts.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126/r10.anchor: ويدخل فيه الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r1.claim: Appetitive desire, anger, and greed impel people away from patience; lifelong struggle to master these blameworthy traits is necessary for patience and muṣābara.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r1.anchor: فيه أخلاقا ذميمة تحمل على أضدادها وهي الشهوة والغضب والحرص

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r2.claim: Since action arises from inner faculties, murābaṭa means struggling against the powers that generate blameworthy deeds; taqwa repels their prompting, and success is the goal that motivates it.

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī says the verse compresses spiritual wisdom and completes the surah’s treatment of foundational beliefs and practical duties.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r3.anchor: هذه الآية التي هي خاتمة لهذه السورة مشتملة على كنوز الحكم والاسرار الروحانية

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to remain patient in religion despite poverty and hunger, and to stand firm against the enemy despite the defeat at Uḥud.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r4.anchor: قال الحسن : اصبروا على دينكم ولا تتركوه بسبب الفقر والجوع

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets the commands as patience alongside the Prophet and steadfastness against the enemy, so Muslims should outlast them.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء : اصبروا مع نبيكم وصابروا عدوكم

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r6.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r6.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the many duties discussed in the surah call for patience, while its repeated encouragement of jihad calls for steadfastness against enemies.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r6.anchor: وقال الأصم : لما كثرت تكاليف الله في هذه السورة أمرهم بالصبر عليها

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r7.claim: One interpretation of murābaṭa is stationing tethered horses at frontier posts, with both sides ready to fight; the author links this to 8:60.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r7.anchor: أنه عبارة عن أن يربط هؤلاء خيلهم في الثغور ويربط أولئك خيلهم أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r8.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r8.claim: A prophetic report says a day and night stationed in God’s cause equals a month of fasting and prayer, without breaking the fast or leaving prayer except for need.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r8.anchor: من رابط يوما وليلة في سبيل الله كان مثل صيام شهر وقيامه

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r9.claim: A second interpretation is waiting for one prayer after another.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r9.anchor: أن معنى المرابطة انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r10.speaker: أبو سلمة عبد الرحمن
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r10.claim: Abū Salama ʿAbd al-Raḥmān says there was no campaign requiring frontier duty in the Prophet’s time, so the verse concerned waiting for the next prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r10.anchor: ما روي عن أبي سلمة عبد الرحمن أنه قال : لم يكن في زمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم غزو

RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r11.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra describes waiting for prayer after prayer and calls this murābaṭa three times.
RAZI-FULL:v9p126#2/r11.anchor: ما روي من حديث أبي هريرة حين ذكر انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة ثم قال : ( فذلكم الرباط ) ثلاث مرات

RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r1.claim: The word can include both frontier service and waiting for prayer: ribāṭ comes from binding, and one may bind one’s heart to what one patiently undertakes.

RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r2.claim: Other interpreters define ribāṭ as persistence and staying firm, which also returns to patience and self-discipline; this steadiness may be in jihad or in prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r2.anchor: الرباط هو اللزوم والثبات ، وهذا المعنى أيضا راجع إلى ما ذكرناه من الصبر

RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī records that he completed the commentary on this surah on Thursday, the first of Rabīʿ al-Ākhir 595 AH.
RAZI-FULL:v9p127/r3.anchor: تم تفسير هذه السورة بفضل الله وإحسانه يوم الخميس أول ربيع الآخر سنة خمس وتسعين وخمسمائة

STUDYQURAN:3:200/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r1.speaker: R, Z
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r1.claim: Be patient and vie in patience share the root ṣ-b-r; the second means outdo the enemy in patience and endurance.
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r1.anchor: the second to a contest of patience in which one should outdo the enemy in patience and endurance (R, Z)

STUDYQURAN:3:200/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r2.claim: Rābiṭū comes from a root meaning tie, fortify, and join; ribāṭ generally conveys firmness and steadfastness, especially taking a frontier post for defense or anticipated attack.
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r2.anchor: the word refers to taking up a border or frontier post (or to the post itself) in defense of the community

STUDYQURAN:3:200/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r3.claim: The martial post is called ribāṭ because one ties or bridles one’s horse, as in the Quranic phrase for tethered horses.
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r3.anchor: it is called ribāṭ because one “ties” or bridles one’s horse

STUDYQURAN:3:200/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r4.speaker: IK, Q
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r4.claim: Hadiths praise a day of ribāṭ above the world and all it contains, and say its merit can continue after death because community defense enables others’ piety.
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r4.anchor: One day of ribāṭ in the way of God is better in God’s Eyes than this world and all that is in it

STUDYQURAN:3:200/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r5.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r5.claim: The Prophet calls ablution in unpleasant conditions, many steps to the mosque, and waiting for one prayer after another ribāṭ.
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r5.anchor: Performing ablutions under unpleasant conditions, multiplying one’s steps to the mosque, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer

STUDYQURAN:3:200/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r6.claim: Waiting between canonical prayers means remaining in remembrance, devotion, and reflection; al-Nawawī compares this spiritual ribāṭ with martial ribāṭ.
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r6.anchor: This is a spiritual ribāṭ, which is compared with the martial ribāṭ by the famous jurist al-Nawawī

STUDYQURAN:3:200/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r7.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r7.claim: A well-known hadith says those returning from battle have come from lesser jihad to greater jihad, which the Prophet identifies as struggle against one’s passions.
STUDYQURAN:3:200/r7.anchor: A servant’s jihād against his passions

TAB-FULL:v6p333/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r1.claim: Believers must hold to their religion in hardship and ease, endure against unbelievers, and guard against polytheists.
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، أنه سمعه يقول في قول الله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا} [آل عمران: 200] قال: «أمرهم أن يصبروا

TAB-FULL:v6p333/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r2.claim: He explains the commands as patience in obeying God, perseverance against misguided people, and frontier service in God's path.
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا} [آل عمران: 200] «أي اصبروا على طاعة الله

TAB-FULL:v6p333/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r3.claim: He glosses patience as obedience, perseverance as facing God's enemies, and ribat as service in God's path.
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج: {اصبروا} [آل عمران: 200] «على الطاعة» {وصابروا} [آل عمران: 200] «أعداء الله

TAB-FULL:v6p333/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r4.claim: He says to persist in what was commanded, persevere against the enemy, and stand guard against them.
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا} [آل عمران: 200] قال: «اصبروا على ما أمرتم به

TAB-FULL:v6p333/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r5.claim: He reads the commands as steadfastness in religion, perseverance for God's promised reward, and standing against God's and the believers' enemies until they leave their religion.
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r5.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي، أنه كان يقول في هذه الآية: {اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا} [آل عمران: 200] يقول: «اصبروا على دينكم

TAB-FULL:v6p333/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r6.claim: He interprets all three commands in the context of jihad: endure jihad, persevere against the enemy, and remain stationed against them.
TAB-FULL:v6p333/r6.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم، في قوله: {اصبروا وصابروا ورابطوا} [آل عمران: 200] قال: «اصبروا على الجهاد

TAB-FULL:v6p334/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r1.claim: In a letter to Abu Ubayda about threatening Roman forces, he says God brings relief after hardship and cites this verse.
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r1.anchor: فكتب إليه عمر: " أما بعد، فإنه مهما نزل بعبد مؤمن منزلة شدة يجعل الله بعدها فرجا

TAB-FULL:v6p334/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r2.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r2.claim: He says ribat meant waiting for one prayer after another, since there was no wartime frontier stationing in the Prophet's time.
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r2.anchor: قال لي أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: يا ابن أخي هل تدري في أي شيء نزلت هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v6p334/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r3.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r3.claim: The Prophet taught that thorough ablution despite difficulty and waiting for the next prayer expiate sins; this is ribat.
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r3.anchor: عن شرحبيل، عن علي، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألا أدلكم على ما يكفر الله به الذنوب

TAB-FULL:v6p334/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r4.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r4.claim: The Prophet taught that thorough ablution, many steps to the mosque, and waiting between prayers erase sins and constitute ribat.
TAB-FULL:v6p334/r4.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو الله به الخطايا

TAB-FULL:v6p336/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r1.claim: The Prophet says thorough ablution despite hardship, frequent steps to mosques, and waiting between prayers remove sins and raise ranks; this is ribat.
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألا أدلكم على ما يحط الله به الخطايا

TAB-FULL:v6p336/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r2.claim: He reads patience broadly as endurance in every kind of obedience, hard or easy, because the verse does not specify an exception.
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r2.anchor: اصبروا على دينكم، وطاعة ربكم، وذلك أن الله لم يخصص من معاني الصبر على الدين والطاعة شيئا

TAB-FULL:v6p336/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r3.claim: He reads صابروا as persevering against polytheist enemies until God grants victory, since reciprocal Arabic forms ordinarily involve two or more parties.
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r3.anchor: المعروف من كلام العرب في المفاعلة، أن تكون من فريقين، أو اثنين فصاعدا

TAB-FULL:v6p336/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r4.claim: He takes رابطوا in its familiar sense of guarding against the enemies of the faith at a frontier.
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r4.anchor: ورابطوا أعداءكم وأعداء دينكم من أهل الشرك في سبيل الله

TAB-FULL:v6p336/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r5.claim: Ribat originally meant tethering horses for an enemy, then came to mean any mounted or foot guard stationed to protect those behind him.
TAB-FULL:v6p336/r5.anchor: وأرى أن أصل الرباط: ارتباط الخيل للعدو، كما ارتبط عدوهم لهم خيلهم، ثم استعمل ذلك في كل مقيم في ثغر

TAB-FULL:v6p338/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p338/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p338/r1.claim: God-fearing means avoiding disobedience to God's commands and not crossing His prohibitions.
TAB-FULL:v6p338/r1.anchor: واحذروه أن تخالفوا أمره، أو تتقدموا نهيه

TAB-FULL:v6p338/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p338/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v6p338/r2.claim: He says believers should fear God in their dealings so they may prosper when they meet Him tomorrow.
TAB-FULL:v6p338/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي، أنه كان يقول في قوله: {واتقوا الله لعلكم تفلحون} [البقرة: 189] «واتقوا الله فيما بيني وبينكم

TABATABAI:3:200/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200/r1.claim: This closing verse summarizes the surah’s detailed instruction and draws its result.
TABATABAI:3:200/r1.anchor: بيان الآية بمنزلة الفذلكة لتفصيل البيان الوارد في السورة

TABATABAI:3:200/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200/r2.claim: The unrestricted command to be patient covers hardship, obedience to God, and avoiding disobedience; its singular form contrasts with collective mutual endurance.
TABATABAI:3:200/r2.anchor: فالصبر يراد به الصبر على الشدائد والصبر في طاعة الله والصبر عن معصيته

TABATABAI:3:200/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200/r3.claim: Mutual patience is shared endurance in which people rely on one another, strengthening the quality and multiplying its effect through cooperation.
TABATABAI:3:200/r3.anchor: والمصابرة هي التصبر وتحمل الأذى جماعة باعتماد صبر البعض على صبر آخرين

TABATABAI:3:200/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200/r4.claim: Ribāṭ is broader: it binds a community’s strengths and actions across all religious affairs in hardship and ease; the commands aim at complete happiness in both worlds, so they conclude with piety and true success.
TABATABAI:3:200/r4.anchor: أعم معنى من المصابرة وهي إيجاد الجماعة الارتباط بين قواهم وأفعالهم

TABATABAI:3:200/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200/r5.claim: Human beings are inherently social, as history, social organization, and several Qur’anic passages affirm; people are made into peoples and tribes to know one another and depend on one another.
TABATABAI:3:200/r5.anchor: كون النوع الإنساني نوعا اجتماعيا لا يحتاج في إثباته إلى كثير بحث فكل فرد من هذا النوع مفطور على ذلك

TABATABAI:3:200#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r1.claim: Human social organization, like other spiritual traits, developed gradually alongside material and moral capacities rather than appearing complete at humanity’s beginning.
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r1.anchor: الاجتماع الإنساني كسائر الخواص الروحية الإنسانية وما يرتبط بها لم يوجد حين وجد تاما كاملا

TABATABAI:3:200#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r2.claim: The earliest form was the household founded through marriage, because reproduction most directly requires more than one person; this grew into “use,” subordinating others to meet one’s needs by imposing authority and will.
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r2.anchor: أول ما ظهر من الاجتماع فيه الاجتماع المنزلي بالازدواج لكون عامله الطبيعي وهو جهاز التناسل

TABATABAI:3:200#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r3.claim: Use developed into household, clan, tribal, and national leadership; the initial leader was chosen by strength and courage, then wealth and descendants, and ultimately skill in government and politics.
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r3.anchor: ثم برز ذلك في صورة الرئاسة كرئيس المنزل ورئيس العشيرة ورئيس القبيلة ورئيس الأمة

TABATABAI:3:200#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r4.claim: This hierarchy was the initial cause of idolatry, according to the author, and has continued to the present.
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r4.anchor: وهذا هو السبب الابتدائي لظهور الوثنية وقيامها على ساقها حتى اليوم

TABATABAI:3:200#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r5.claim: Society persisted through these stages without people consciously isolating it as a value; it grew under other concerns such as use and defense, until prophecy first drew explicit attention to preserving it.
TABATABAI:3:200#2/r5.anchor: أول ما نبه الإنسان بالاجتماع تفصيلا واعتنى بحفظه استقلالا نبهته به النبوة

TABATABAI:3:200#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r1.claim: Humanity began as one simple community; conflicts later arose, prompting prophets and revealed books to restore social unity through law.
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r1.anchor: كان أمة واحدة ساذجة لا اختلاف بينهم حتى ظهرت الاختلافات وبانت المشاجرات

TABATABAI:3:200#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r2.claim: The Qur’an presents establishing religion and avoiding division as the means by which prophetic teaching unifies people.
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r2.anchor: رفع الاختلاف من بين الناس وإيجاد الاتحاد في كلمتهم إنما كان في صورة الدعوة إلى إقامة الدين

TABATABAI:3:200#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r3.claim: The social-unity call is traced through Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus; Noah’s and Abraham’s laws were limited, Moses’ broader, and Jesus’ followed Moses’ law.
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r3.anchor: وقد كان في شريعة نوح وإبراهيم النزر اليسير من الأحكام وأوسع هؤلاء الأربعة شريعة موسى

TABATABAI:3:200#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r4.claim: Islam uniquely made social organization an explicit foundation and comprehensively shaped human activity through communal rules.
TABATABAI:3:200#3/r4.anchor: الإسلام هو الدين الوحيد الذي أسس بنيانه على الاجتماع صريحا ولم يهمل أمر الاجتماع في شأن من شؤونه

TABATABAI:3:200#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r1.claim: Ancient and other established societies generally inherited social order through subordination to rulers, monarchy, and factors such as lineage and place.
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r1.anchor: كانت تتبع ما ورثته من أقدم عهود الإنسانية من استتباع الاجتماع بالاستخدام

TABATABAI:3:200#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r2.claim: Greek philosophers discussed society, but their ideas remained speculative writings without practical historical application.
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r2.anchor: إلا أنها كانت أوراقا وصحائف لا ترد مورد العمل، ومثلا ذهنية لا تنزل مرحلة العين والخارج

TABATABAI:3:200#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r3.claim: Islam first called humanity to treat social organization as an independent concern and seek collective well-being.
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r3.anchor: فأول نداء قرع سمع النوع الإنساني ودعى به هذا النوع إلى الاعتناء بأمر الاجتماع

TABATABAI:3:200#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r4.claim: Qur’anic commands preserve communal unity by following the straight path and avoiding divisive rival paths.
TABATABAI:3:200#4/r4.anchor: وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم

TABATABAI:3:200#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r1.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly calls for social unity and cohesion and warns against religious factionalism.
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r1.anchor: إلى غير ذلك من الآيات المطلقة الداعية إلى أصل الاجتماع والاتحاد

TABATABAI:3:200#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r2.claim: Believers are brothers and must reconcile disputes between fellow believers.
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r2.anchor: إنما المؤمنون إخوة فأصلحوا بين أخويكم

TABATABAI:3:200#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r3.claim: Internal conflict weakens the community and dissipates its collective strength.

TABATABAI:3:200#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r4.claim: The community is commanded to cooperate in virtue and piety.

TABATABAI:3:200#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r5.claim: Islamic society is to unite in securing shared material and spiritual benefits and defending the community.
TABATABAI:3:200#5/r5.anchor: بناء المجتمع الإسلامي على الاتفاق والاتحاد في حيازة منافعها ومزاياها المعنوية والمادية والدفاع عنه

TABATABAI:3:200#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r1.claim: The Qur’an grounds social bonds in shared human origins and kinship, describing humanity as created from water and joined by lineage and marriage.
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r1.anchor: خلق من الماء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا

TABATABAI:3:200#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r2.claim: The Qur’an addresses people as created from a male and a female, supporting a common basis for human society.
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r2.anchor: يا أيها الناس إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى

TABATABAI:3:200#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r3.claim: The statement that people are from one another expresses their real mutual bond.
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r3.anchor: وقال بعضكم من بعض آل عمران 195

TABATABAI:3:200#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r4.claim: The real bond between a person and society gives society a distinct collective existence shaped by its members’ powers and effects.
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r4.anchor: وهذه الرابطة الحقيقية بين الشخص والمجتمع لا محالة تؤدي إلى كينونة أخرى في المجتمع

TABATABAI:3:200#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r5.claim: The Qur’an attributes existence, a lifespan, a book, understanding, deeds, obedience, and disobedience to communities as collective subjects.
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r5.anchor: اعتبر القرآن للأمة وجودا وأجلا وكتابا وشعورا وفهما وعملا وطاعة ومعصية

TABATABAI:3:200#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r6.claim: Unlike earlier historians focused on rulers and notable individuals, historians began attending to peoples and societies after the Qur’an.
TABATABAI:3:200#6/r6.anchor: ولم يشتغل المؤرخون بتواريخ الأمم والمجتمعات إلا بعد نزول القرآن

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r1.claim: Collective powers can overpower individual dispositions, as crowds and social attacks suppress dissenting individual will.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r1.anchor: قوى وخواص اجتماعية قوية تقهر القوى والخواص الفردية عند التعارض والتضاد

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r2.claim: Collective panic, defeat, insecurity, and even customary fashions can suppress an individual’s thought and perception.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r2.anchor: حتى أنه يسلب الشعور والفكر من أفراده وأجزائه

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r3.claim: Because social forces shape individuals, Islam organizes major duties such as pilgrimage, prayer, jihad, and giving around communal life.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r3.anchor: فوضع أهم أحكامه وشرائعه كالحج والصلاة والجهاد والإنفاق

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r4.claim: Islam adds government enforcement and a duty on the whole community to call to good and forbid wrong.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r4.anchor: ومضافا إلى فريضة الدعوة إلى الخير والأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر العامة لجميع الامة

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r5.claim: The community’s shared aim is real happiness and nearness to God, providing an inner oversight beyond outward monitoring.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r5.anchor: السعادة الحقيقية والقرب والمنزلة عند الله

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r6.claim: He anticipates the objection that Islam’s supposedly superior social order lasted briefly before turning into caliphal and imperial despotism, unlike durable Western civilization.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r6.anchor: فما باله لم يقبل الإجراء إلا برهة يسيرة ثم لم يملك نفسه دون أن تبدل قيصرية وكسروية

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r7.claim: The objection treats modern civil society’s longevity and social order as evidence that its system is more advanced and durable.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r7.anchor: وهذا هو الدليل على كون مدنيتهم أرقى وسنتهم في الاجتماع أتقن وأشد استحكاما

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r8.claim: Modern systems are said to rest on popular preference and majority rule, on the premise that nature’s causes usually prevail more often than they do not.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r8.anchor: وقد وضعوا سنتهم الاجتماعية وقوانينهم الدائرة على أساس إرادة الامة واقتراح الطباع والميول

TABATABAI:3:200#7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r9.claim: The objection claims that natural causes usually operate according to majority outcomes rather than without exception.
TABATABAI:3:200#7/r9.anchor: فإنا نجد كلا من العلل المادية والأسباب الطبيعية مؤثرة على الأكثر لا على الدوام

TABATABAI:3:200#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r1.claim: The argument credits modern civilization with social strength and happiness and with refining individuals away from socially condemned vices.
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r1.anchor: وقد ضمنت المدنية الحاضرة فيما ظهرت فيه من الممالك قوة المجتمع وسعادتها وتهذب الأفراد وطهارتهم من الرذائل

TABATABAI:3:200#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this objection reflects views common among Eastern researchers but that they approach the question from the wrong starting point.
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r2.anchor: وهذا الذي أوردناه محصل ما يختلج في صدور جمع من باحثينا معاشر الشرقيين

TABATABAI:3:200#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r3.claim: Some researchers claim that Islamic social law cannot operate under present conditions, unlike modern civil systems.
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r3.anchor: أما قولهم إن السنة الاجتماعية الإسلامية غير قابلة الجريان في الدنيا على خلاف سنن المدنية الحاضرة

TABATABAI:3:200#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r4.claim: New social systems commonly arise under conditions hostile to them, may be resisted and defeated at first, and can later prevail or disappear depending on circumstances.
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r4.anchor: فإن جميع السنن الدائرة في الجامعة الإنسانية إنما حدثت بعد ما لم تكن وظهرت في حين لم تكن عامة الأوضاع

TABATABAI:3:200#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r5.claim: A social order’s mismatch with current conditions does not show it is false; the Qur’an points to historical outcomes as a guide.
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r5.anchor: فمجرد عدم انطباق سنة من السنن على الوضع الإنساني الحاضر ليس يكشف عن بطلانه وفساده

TABATABAI:3:200#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r6.claim: Islam has taken root in over four hundred million people, and its present position is no weaker than its beginnings with a single follower in prophetic missions.
TABATABAI:3:200#8/r6.anchor: وقد تمكن في نفوس ما يزيد على أربعمائة مليون من أفراد البشر ونشب في قلوبهم

TABATABAI:3:200#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r1.claim: Prophetic movements began with very few supporters, faced hardship, and grew through successive converts into communities marked by righteousness.
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r1.anchor: ولم يكن معه من يستظهر به يومئذ إلا رجل وامرأة ثم لم يزل يلحق بهم واحد بعد واحد

TABATABAI:3:200#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r2.claim: The early Muslim community remained socially righteous for a time, until later disorders arose after the Prophet’s death.
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r2.anchor: ومكثوا برهة على الصلاح الاجتماعي حتى كان من أمر الفتن بعد رسول الله

TABATABAI:3:200#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r3.claim: Within less than half a century, Islam spread east and west and transformed history, with effects that continue.
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r3.anchor: لم يلبث حتى انبسط في أقل من نصف قرن على مشارق الأرض ومغاربها وحول التاريخ تحويلا جوهريا

TABATABAI:3:200#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says Islam’s emergence was the proximate and complete cause of modern civilizational transformation, while European neglect reflects religious or political bias.
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r4.anchor: المنشأ القريب والعامل التام للتحول المعاصر المشهود في الدنيا هو ظهور السنة الإسلامية

TABATABAI:3:200#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r5.claim: Calling modern civilizational progress Christian is misguided because Jesus disclaimed concern with bodily, state, and political affairs, whereas Islam addresses all social affairs.
TABATABAI:3:200#9/r5.anchor: والمسيح يصرح بأنه إنما يهتم بأمر الروح ولا يشتغل بأمر الجسم ولا يتعرض لشأن الدولة والسياسة

TABATABAI:3:200#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r1.claim: Humanity is ultimately expected to reach Islam’s full realization and its complete direction of human society.
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r1.anchor: كمال ظهور الإسلام بحقيقته في الدنيا وتوليه التام أمر المجتمع الإنساني

TABATABAI:3:200#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r2.claim: The Qur’an promises a people who love God, strive in His path, and fear no blame.
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r2.anchor: فسوف يأتي الله بقوم يحبهم ويحبونه أذلة على المؤمنين أعزة على الكافرين

TABATABAI:3:200#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r3.claim: The Qur’an also promises believers succession, security, and an established religion, and says the righteous will inherit the earth.
TABATABAI:3:200#10/r3.anchor: ليستخلفنهم في الأرض كما استخلف الذين من قبلهم وليمكنن لهم دينهم

TABATABAI:3:200#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r1.claim: Islam’s social order takes truth as its sole guiding principle, whereas modern civil society follows majority opinion and desire.
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r1.anchor: الاجتماع الإسلامي شعاره الوحيد هو اتباع الحق في النظر والعمل والاجتماع المدني الحاضر شعاره اتباع ما يراه ويريده الأكثر

TABATABAI:3:200#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r2.claim: Islam aims at true intellectual happiness by balancing bodily needs under worship and making social life support knowledge of God.
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r2.anchor: غاية الاجتماع الإسلامي السعادة الحقيقية العقلية بمعنى أن يأخذ الإنسان بالاعتدال في مقتضيات قواه

TABATABAI:3:200#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r3.claim: Islamic law appeals to sound reason and entrusts society, as well as government, with carrying out law, ethics, and foundational beliefs.
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r3.anchor: وألقى ضمان إجراء الجميع من الأعمال والأخلاق والمعارف الأصلية إلى عهدة المجتمع

TABATABAI:3:200#11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r4.claim: This moral program conflicts with common appetites and requires sustained preaching and education.
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r4.anchor: إلا بعد مجاهدة شديدة في نشر الدعوة وبسط التربية

TABATABAI:3:200#11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r5.claim: Modern civil law instead serves material enjoyment, following popular desires except where they obstruct that aim.
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r5.anchor: غاية الاجتماع المدني الحاضر فهي التمتع من المادة

TABATABAI:3:200#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r6.claim: Modern law regulates conduct but leaves morality and foundational knowledge without a guarantor, allowing appetite and anger to shape social norms.
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r6.anchor: وأما الأخلاق والمعارف الأصلية فلا ضامن لإجرائها

TABATABAI:3:200#11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r7.claim: A sensory society can rebrand religiously condemned behavior as virtue and mock religious norms because its standards of thought differ.
TABATABAI:3:200#11/r7.anchor: فربما كان الفجور والفسق في مجرى العقل تقوى في مجرى الميول والإحساسات

TABATABAI:3:200#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r1.claim: Western civilization is not uniquely suited to human nature; societies across history generally favor materialistic systems over religion because of material idolatry.
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r1.anchor: جميع السنن المعمولة الدائرة في الدنيا بين أهلها من أقدم أعصار الإنسانية إلى عصرنا هذا

TABATABAI:3:200#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r2.claim: Modern civilization recasts ancient pagan practices from individual life into collective systems and from simplicity into technical complexity.
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r2.anchor: ليست إلا مؤلفة من سنن الوثنية الاولى غير أنها تحولت من حال الفردية إلى حال الاجتماع

TABATABAI:3:200#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r3.claim: The Qur’an repeatedly defines Islam’s standard as truth, even though most people dislike truth.
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r3.anchor: لقد جئناكم بالحق ولكن أكثركم للحق كارهون

TABATABAI:3:200#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r4.claim: Following people’s desires would corrupt the heavens, earth, and all within them; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī points readers to Sūrat Yūnus for its repeated emphasis on truth.
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r4.anchor: ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم لفسدت السماوات والأرض ومن فيهن

TABATABAI:3:200#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r5.claim: Nature’s tendency toward outcomes that occur most often does not negate the duty to follow truth, since nature itself is one instance of truth.
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r5.anchor: فإنها نفسها بعض مصاديق الحق فكيف تبطل نفسها؟

TABATABAI:3:200#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r6.claim: External causal regularities are constant; even events that occur mostly follow a stable, enduring pattern, as with fire’s usual heating effect.
TABATABAI:3:200#12/r6.anchor: أثر دائم لها وهكذا وهذا هو الحق

TABATABAI:3:200#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r1.claim: Human beings naturally submit to what they recognize as objectively real; even a skeptic accepts a self-evident proposition when confronted with it.
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r1.anchor: الإنسان بحسب الفطرة يتبع ما وجده أمرا واقعيا خارجيا بنحو

TABATABAI:3:200#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r2.claim: Truth is the external reality people believe or follow; perception is only a means of access, like a mirror to what it reflects.
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r2.anchor: وأما نظر الإنسان وإدراكه فإنما هو وسيلة يتوسل بها اليه كالمرآة بالنسبة إلى المرئي

TABATABAI:3:200#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r3.claim: Truth as permanence or frequent occurrence belongs to the external object, not to knowledge or perception.
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r3.anchor: إنما هي صفة الخارج الواقع وقوعا دائميا أو أكثريا دون العلم والإدراك

TABATABAI:3:200#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r4.claim: Majority opinions may match reality or fail to match it, so they are not inherently true or binding.
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r4.anchor: وأما آراء الأكثرين وأنظارهم واعتقاداتهم في مقابل الأقلين فليست بحق دائما

TABATABAI:3:200#13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r5.claim: Someone convinced of a fact does not naturally submit to a contrary majority view; outward conformity may instead come from fear or shame.
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r5.anchor: فإنك إذا أيقنت بأمر ثم خالفك جميع الناس فيه لم تخضع بالطبع لنظرهم

TABATABAI:3:200#13/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r6.claim: The Qur’an’s statement that most people dislike truth demonstrates that a majority can oppose what is true.
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r6.anchor: بل جاءهم بالحق وأكثرهم للحق كارهون

TABATABAI:3:200#13/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r7.claim: Human action follows frequent outcomes in external reality, not majority opinion; Qur’anic legislation likewise builds on prevalent practical benefit.
TABATABAI:3:200#13/r7.anchor: إنما هو ما في الخارج من أكثرية الوقوع لا ما اعتقده الأكثرون

TABATABAI:3:200#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r1.claim: Qur’anic laws account for predominant benefits, as shown by the aims of removing hardship, purification, completing divine favor, and fostering gratitude.
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r1.anchor: إلى غير ذلك من الآيات المشتملة على ملاكات غالبية الوقوع للأحكام المشرعة

TABATABAI:3:200#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r2.claim: The Qur’an describes law as intended to remove hardship, purify people, complete divine favor, and foster gratitude.
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r2.anchor: ما يريد الله ليجعل عليكم من حرج ولكن يريد ليطهركم وليتم نعمته عليكم

TABATABAI:3:200#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r3.claim: Fasting is prescribed as it was for earlier communities so that believers may attain piety; such laws address likely outcomes.
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r3.anchor: كتب عليكم الصيام كما كتب على الذين من قبلكم لعلكم تتقون

TABATABAI:3:200#14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r4.claim: Material strength and wealth are not, by themselves, human happiness; true happiness joins bodily well-being with spiritual virtues and divine knowledge for both lives.
TABATABAI:3:200#14/r4.anchor: السعادة الانسانية أمر مؤلف من سعادة الروح والبدن

TABATABAI:3:200#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r1.claim: Some Eastern researchers mistake European social virtues because they think individually rather than considering society as a unified person.
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r1.anchor: جل المتفكرين من باحثينا معاشر الشرقيين لا يقدرون على التفكر الاجتماعي وإنما يتفكرون تفكرا فرديا

TABATABAI:3:200#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r2.claim: An individual thinker sees himself as independent and pursues personal benefit, then wrongly assumes other people operate by the same outlook.
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r2.anchor: فلا يشتغل إلا بشأن نفسه وهو التفكر الفردي ويستتبع ذلك أن يقيس غيره على نفسه

TABATABAI:3:200#15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r3.claim: A social thinker sees personal interests as inseparable from the community’s interests and treats communal good and harm as his own.
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r3.anchor: يرى خير المجتمع خير نفسه وشره شر نفسه

TABATABAI:3:200#15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r4.claim: The human body illustrates social unity: organs serve the whole and ordinarily do not harm one another while acting under one human identity.
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r4.anchor: وأما معاملة بعضها مع بعض والجميع تحت لواء الانسانية الواحدة فقلما يتفق أن يسيء بعضها إلى بعض

TABATABAI:3:200#15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r5.claim: The Qur’an judges peoples collectively, rebuking present generations for earlier members’ deeds when they share a group identity and social outlook.
TABATABAI:3:200#15/r5.anchor: يؤاخذ اللاحقين بذنوب السابقين ويعاتب الحاضرين ويوبخهم بأعمال الغائبين والماضين

TABATABAI:3:200#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r1.claim: Fairness requires exempting genuinely righteous individuals from collective blame when they live within a corrupt society.
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r1.anchor: أن لا يضطهد حق الصالحين من الأفراد بذلك إن وجدوا في مجتمع واحد

TABATABAI:3:200#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r2.claim: Judge developed societies by their outward dealings with other peoples, not only by cordial relations among their own members.
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r2.anchor: بل بالبناء على شخصيتهم الاجتماعية البارزة في مماستها ومصاكتها سائر الامم الضعيفة

TABATABAI:3:200#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī alleges that European powers profess service and liberty while subjugating weak peoples through force, colonialism, and other pretexts.
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r3.anchor: لا هم لهم إلا استعباد الامم الضعيفة مساكين الأرض ما وجدوا إليه سبيلا

TABATABAI:3:200#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r4.claim: A society that exploits others cannot be judged righteous or happy by sound human nature; if its condition is called happiness, it means domination.
TABATABAI:3:200#16/r4.anchor: فإن سمي ما عندهم سعادة وصلاحا فلتكن بمعنى التحكم وإطلاق المشيئة

TABATABAI:3:200#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r1.claim: Every society forms around a common purpose that functions as its shared spirit.
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r1.anchor: إنما يتحقق ويحصل بوجود غاية واحدة مشتركة بين أفراده المتشتتة

TABATABAI:3:200#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r2.claim: Nonreligious societies unite around collectively enjoying material life, whereas an isolated person would face fewer external limits on enjoyment.
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r2.anchor: وهي التمتع من مزايا الحياة المادية على نحو الاجتماع

TABATABAI:3:200#17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r3.claim: Individual physical limits restrain some activities, but another person would not restrict a solitary person in a hypothetical world without competition for resources.
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r3.anchor: فلا سبب هناك يقتضي تضييق ميدان عمله ولا تحديد فعل من أفعاله

TABATABAI:3:200#17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r4.claim: In society, unrestricted personal will causes competition and conflict that corrupt life and threaten human survival.
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r4.anchor: لأدى ذلك إلى التمانع والتزاحم الذي فيه فساد العيش وهلاك النوع

TABATABAI:3:200#17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r5.claim: Primitive customs emerge from conflict and remain unstable, while developed societies deliberately create rules and enforcement power.
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r5.anchor: يرفعون به التضاد والتمانع الواقع بين الارادات وأعمال المجتمع بتعديلها بوضع حدود وقيود لها

TABATABAI:3:200#17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r6.claim: Law is the adjustment of people’s wills and actions through limits that remove conflict and competition.
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r6.anchor: أن القانون حقيقة هو ما تعدل به إرادات الناس وأعمالهم برفع التزاحم والتمانع من بينهما

TABATABAI:3:200#17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r7.claim: People remain free outside the areas governed by law, which is why contemporary laws often leave theology and ethics unregulated.
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r7.anchor: القوانين الحاضرة لا تتعرض لأمر المعارف الإلهية والأخلاق

TABATABAI:3:200#17/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r8.claim: When religion is left dependent on law, it becomes outward custom, and politics alternately suppresses, promotes, or ignores it as convenient.
TABATABAI:3:200#17/r8.anchor: فيوما تقضي عليه وتدحضه ويوما تميل إليه فتبالغ في إعلاء كلمته

TABATABAI:3:200#18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r1.claim: The objection says Islam’s present weakness reflects a lack of someone to enforce its prescriptions.
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r1.anchor: وليس إلا لفقدانه من يحمل نواميسه على الناس يوما

TABATABAI:3:200#18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r2.claim: All general laws, divine or human, are mental forms and only become operative in practice through human will.
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r2.anchor: حقيقة القوانين العامة سواء كانت إلهية أو بشرية ليست إلا صورا ذهنية في أذهان الناس

TABATABAI:3:200#18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r3.claim: Civil law links conduct to majority will but does not concern itself with preserving that will’s effectiveness.
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r3.anchor: والقوانين المدنية لا تهتم بأزيد من تعليق الأفعال بالإرادات

TABATABAI:3:200#18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r4.claim: Law fails when the majority will decays, loses awareness through luxury, or is overpowered by an autocrat.
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r4.anchor: وإذا ماتت من جهة انحطاط يعرض لنفوس الناس وهرم يطرأ على بنية المجتمع

TABATABAI:3:200#18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r5.claim: Civil law has no ultimate safeguard if its enforcers turn public authority into personal domination; history supplies many examples.
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r5.anchor: لم يكن هناك ما يقهر هذا القاهر فيحوله إلى مجراه العدل

TABATABAI:3:200#18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r6.claim: Enforcement also fails when violations are hidden or fall outside the enforcers’ jurisdiction.
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r6.anchor: خفاء نقض القانون على القوة المجرية أحيانا أو خروجه عن حومة قدرته

TABATABAI:3:200#18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r7.claim: Islam unifies society around monotheism and the afterlife, grounding law, worship, true knowledge, virtue, justice, and social life in one connected purpose.
TABATABAI:3:200#18/r7.anchor: أخذ أعني الإسلام الغاية التي يتكون عليها المجتمع البشري ويتوحد بها دين التوحيد

TABATABAI:3:200#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r1.claim: Civil law cannot secure the community where crimes remain unknown or occur beyond its reach; the world wars illustrate social disintegration.
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r1.anchor: في جميع هذه الموارد لا تنال الامة امنيتها من جريان القانون وانحفاظ المجتمع عن التفاسد والتلاشي

TABATABAI:3:200#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r2.claim: Political will needs high moral character to remain effective; without that foundation, social law resembles a tree uprooted from the ground.
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r2.anchor: لأن المجتمع لم يهتم بالسبب الحافظ لإرادات الامة على قوتها وسيطرتها وهي الأخلاق العالية

TABATABAI:3:200#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī describes communism as a product of democracy’s inequality, luxury, deprivation, and resulting resentment.
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r3.anchor: فليست إلا من مواليد الديموقراطية أنتجها إتراف طبقة من طبقات المجتمع وحرمان آخرين

TABATABAI:3:200#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r4.claim: He attributes repeated world wars and their devastation to arrogance, greed, and acquisitiveness.
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r4.anchor: ولا عامل لها إلا غريزة الاستكبار والشره والطمع

TABATABAI:3:200#19/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r5.claim: Islam grounds law in moral education, giving it inward reach through private and public life beyond the reach of police.
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r5.anchor: فهي مع الإنسان في سره وعلانيته وخلوته وجلوته تؤدي وظيفتها

TABATABAI:3:200#19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r6.claim: Modern moral education is contradictory because unrestricted material indulgence creates excess and deprivation, while societies preach virtue yet exploit weaker peoples.
TABATABAI:3:200#19/r6.anchor: فهل الدعوة الى فضائل الأخلاق والترغيب عليها إلا دعوة الى المتناقضين

TABATABAI:3:200#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r1.claim: Virtue needs a guarantor, which al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī identifies as belief in one God who loves good, hates corruption, and will judge and reward everyone.
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r1.anchor: وليس الا التوحيد - أعني القول بأن للعالم إلها واحدا ذا أسماء حسنى

TABATABAI:3:200#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r2.claim: Without belief in the afterlife, no fundamental restraint prevents people from pursuing self-interest at another’s expense.
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r2.anchor: لولا الاعتقاد بالمعاد لم يكن هناك سبب أصيل رادع عن اتباع الهوى

TABATABAI:3:200#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r3.claim: Patriotism, humanitarian feeling, and public praise are unstable emotions, not reliable guarantees for self-sacrifice if death ends all existence.
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r3.anchor: فإنما هي عواطف قلبية ونزوعات باطنية لا سبب حافظا عليها إلا التعليم والتربية

TABATABAI:3:200#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r4.claim: The promise of posthumous fame can delude people into imagining they will enjoy praise after death, like someone acting under intoxication.
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r4.anchor: فإنما هو غرور يغتر به وخدعة ينخدع بها بهيجان إحساساته وعواطفه

TABATABAI:3:200#20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r5.claim: Monotheism and judgment support ethical conduct even when no one sees, praises, or enforces it, because God knows each deed and will repay it.
TABATABAI:3:200#20/r5.anchor: فإن معه الله العليم الحفيظ القائم على كل نفس بما كسبت

TABATABAI:3:200#21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r1.claim: Sensory motivation urges action only when worldly benefit is felt; rational motivation follows truth whether or not material benefit is perceived.
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r1.anchor: فإذا قارن الفعل نفع وأحس به الإنسان فالإحساس متوقد شديد التوقان

TABATABAI:3:200#21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r2.speaker: عنترة
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r2.claim: Antarah’s verse urges steadfastness in danger for either public praise if killed or relief if he defeats the enemy.

TABATABAI:3:200#21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r3.claim: Qur’anic reasoning trusts God’s guardianship and treats either outcome in battle as one of two good ends.
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r3.anchor: قل لن يصيبنا إلا ما كتب الله لنا هو مولانا وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون

TABATABAI:3:200#21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r4.claim: For believers, every hardship or effort in God’s path is recorded as a good deed, so either victory or death brings reward and ultimate happiness.
TABATABAI:3:200#21/r4.anchor: إلا كتب لهم به عمل صالح إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين

TABATABAI:3:200#22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r1.claim: Antarah’s sensory logic fails whenever action brings neither recognition nor personal relief, leaving no reason to do what is right.
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r1.anchor: فليس بهذا المنطق إلا العي واللكنة

TABATABAI:3:200#22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r2.claim: Self-serving people excuse betrayal, crime, evasion of law, and failure to defend justice by predicting personal loss or ridicule.
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r2.anchor: هذه الموارد المعدودة هي الأسباب العامة في كل بغي وخيانة وجناية

TABATABAI:3:200#22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r3.claim: Islamic motivation makes God’s approval and truth primary while worldly outcomes remain secondary, and applies whether people witness or praise the deed.
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r3.anchor: وإنما يتعلق الغرض بالغايات والمقاصد الدنيوية في المرتبة التالية وبالقصد الثاني

TABATABAI:3:200#22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r4.claim: The Prophet’s companions sometimes confessed crimes and accepted punishments, even death, seeking divine approval and purification.
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r4.anchor: يعترفون عنده بجرائمهم وجناياتهم بالتوبة ويذوقون مر الحدود التي تقام عليهم القتل فما دونه

TABATABAI:3:200#22/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r5.claim: Such episodes show the striking effect of religious teaching in making people surrender even life and its accompanying pleasures.
TABATABAI:3:200#22/r5.anchor: عجيب تأثير البيان الديني في نفوس الناس وتعويده لهم السماحة في ألذ الأشياء وأعزها عندهم

TABATABAI:3:200#23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r1.claim: Some object that pursuing afterlife reward would suppress worldly aims, damage social order, and lead to monasticism.
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r1.anchor: أن جعل الأجر الاخروي وهو الغرض العام في حياة الإنسان الاجتماعية يوجب سقوط الأغراض الحيوية

TABATABAI:3:200#23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls this objection a misunderstanding of divine wisdom and Qur’anic teaching.
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r2.anchor: لكنه توهم ناشئ من الجهل بالحكمة الإلهية والأسرار

TABATABAI:3:200#23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r3.claim: Islamic law follows the created human nature and the causal order, as the Qur’an identifies the upright religion with God’s unaltered creation.
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r3.anchor: فطرة الله التي فطر الناس عليها لا تبديل لخلق الله ذلك الدين القيم

TABATABAI:3:200#23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r4.claim: Human life should align with the real causes that direct humanity toward its intended living purpose; God is their ultimate source, so submission to Him is required.
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r4.anchor: الواجب على الإنسان الإسلام له والخضوع لأمره وهذا معنى كون التوحيد هو الأساس الوحيد للدين الإسلامي

TABATABAI:3:200#23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r5.claim: Submission to God means honoring every proper cause and giving each its due; Muslims pursue worldly and afterlife goals without excessive attachment to either.
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r5.anchor: وله مقاصد مادية وأخرى معنوية لكنه لا يعتني في أمرها بأزيد مما ينبغي من الاعتناء والاهتمام

TABATABAI:3:200#23/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r6.claim: He rejects the claim that religion’s sole purpose is social justice and worship merely secondary: that removes monotheism and reduces religious aims to secular enjoyment.
TABATABAI:3:200#23/r6.anchor: فيه إرجاع للغاية الدينية التي هي كلمة التوحيد إلى الغاية المدنية التي هي التمتع

TABATABAI:3:200#24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r1.claim: The term freedom in its modern political sense became common only in recent centuries, though people long desired the idea.
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r1.anchor: كلمة الحرية على ما يراد بها من المعنى لا يتجاوز عمرها في دورانها على الألسن عدة قرون

TABATABAI:3:200#24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r2.claim: Human freedom naturally arises from the will that moves a person to act; eliminating it destroys sensation, consciousness, and humanity.
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r2.anchor: فإنها حالة نفسية في إبطالها إبطال الحس والشعور المنجر إلى إبطال الإنسانية

TABATABAI:3:200#24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r3.claim: Because humans are social, the same nature that gives them free will requires law to coordinate and limit it.
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r3.anchor: فالطبيعة التي أعطته إطلاق الإرادة والعمل هي بعينها تحدد الإرادة والعمل وتقيد ذلك الإطلاق الابتدائي

TABATABAI:3:200#24/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r4.claim: Modern civil law, grounded in material enjoyment, leaves religion, morality, and conduct outside its legal limits to individual choice.
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r4.anchor: لما وضعت بناء أحكامها على أساس التمتع المادي كما عرفت أنتج ذلك حرية الأمة في أمر المعارف الأصلية الدينية

TABATABAI:3:200#24/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r5.claim: Islam regulates human conduct through divine law based on monotheism and virtue, so it does not permit freedom as exemption from religious norms.
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r5.anchor: فلا شيء مما يتعلق بالإنسان أو يتعلق به الإنسان إلا وللشرع الإسلامي فيه قدم أو أثر قدم

TABATABAI:3:200#24/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r6.claim: Islam's expansive liberty is freedom from servitude to anyone besides God.
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r6.anchor: نعم للإنسان فيه الحرية عن قيد عبودية غير الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:3:200#24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r7.claim: Within law, Islam permits wholesome provisions and balanced life without excess or neglect.
TABATABAI:3:200#24/r7.anchor: التوسعة فيما أباحه الله من طيبات الرزق ومزايا الحياة المعتدلة من غير إفراط أو تفريط

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r1.claim: Islam allows God's adornment and good provisions, and makes earthly and heavenly resources available to people.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r1.anchor: قل من حرم زينة الله التي أخرج لعباده والطيبات من الرزق

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r2.speaker: بعض الباحثين والمفسرين
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r2.claim: Some researchers and exegetes appeal to “no compulsion in religion” and similar verses to assert religious freedom.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r2.anchor: ما رامه بعض الباحثين والمفسرين وتكلف فيه من إثبات حرية العقيدة في الإسلام بقوله تعالى

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r3.claim: Since monotheism underlies every Islamic law, doctrinal freedom would contradict the religion's foundation, like exemption from civil law.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r3.anchor: فليس القول بحرية العقيدة إلا كالقول بالحرية عن حكومة القانون في القوانين المدنية بعينه

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r4.claim: Belief as a cognitive assent formed in the mind is not a voluntary act that can be forbidden, permitted, enslaved, or liberated.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r4.anchor: العقيدة بمعنى حصول إدراك تصديقي ينعقد في ذهن الإنسان ليس عملا اختياريا للإنسان

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r5.claim: Law can govern actions entailed by belief, including preaching, persuading, publishing, and undermining others' beliefs.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r5.anchor: هو الالتزام بما تستوجبه العقيدة من الأعمال كالدعوة إلى العقيدة وإقناع الناس بها

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r6.claim: Islamic doctrine centers on monotheism, prophethood, and resurrection, which the author says unite Muslims, Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians among scriptural communities.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r6.anchor: التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد وهو الذي يجتمع عليه المسلمون واليهود والنصارى والمجوس أهل الكتاب

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r7.claim: A further liberty exists in displaying belief within a course of inquiry, a topic the author postpones to a later chapter.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r7.anchor: نعم ها هنا حرية أخرى وهي الحرية من حيث إظهار العقيدة في مجرى البحث

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r8.speaker: المعترض
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r8.claim: An objection says comprehensive Islamic law and the absence of creed freedom freeze society, while progress needs opposing ideas to clash.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r8.anchor: فإن السير التكاملي يحتاج إلى تحقق القوى المتضادة في الشيء وتفاعلها

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r9.claim: The stagnation objection reflects dialectical materialism and confuses adaptable technical knowledge with foundational metaphysical knowledge.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r9.anchor: أقول وهو من إشكالات المادية التحولية ماترياليسم ديالكتيك وفيه خلط عجيب

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r10.claim: Technical and industrial sciences can change and develop, thereby advancing material social life; Islam does not obstruct them.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r10.anchor: وهذه العلوم والصناعات وما في عدادها كلما تحولت من النقص إلى الكمال أوجب ذلك تحول الحياة الاجتماعية

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r11.claim: Universal theological truths remain fixed while admitting deeper understanding; their stability does not halt social progress.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r11.anchor: وهذه العلوم والمعارف لا تؤثر في الاجتماعات وسنن الحياة إلا بنحو كلي فوقوف هذه المعارف والآراء وثبوتها على حال واحد لا يوجب وقوف الاجتماعات

TABATABAI:3:200#25/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r12.claim: The principle that one God established prophetic law and final judgment is foundational to Islam; denying it degrades society.
TABATABAI:3:200#25/r12.anchor: وهذه هي الكلمة الوحيدة التي بنى عليها الإسلام مجتمعه وتحفظ عليها كل التحفظ

TABATABAI:3:200#26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r1.claim: Society advances through continual industrial research and applying knowledge to practice, which Islam permits.
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r1.anchor: وهذا إنما يتحقق بالبحث الصناعي المداوم وتطبيق العمل على العلم دائما والإسلام لا يمنع من ذلك شيئا

TABATABAI:3:200#26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r2.claim: Political systems change when deficient; their difference is error versus correctness, not necessarily lower versus higher development.
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r2.anchor: فالفرق بينها لو كان فإنما هو فرق الغلط والصواب لا فرق الناقص والكامل

TABATABAI:3:200#26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r3.claim: A just social order, good education, useful knowledge, and virtuous action can support continuing happiness without further institutional change.
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r3.anchor: فإذا استقر أمر السنة الاجتماعية على ما يقصده الإنسان بفطرته وهو العدالة الاجتماعية واستظل الناس تحت التربية الجيدة بالعلم النافع والعمل الصالح

TABATABAI:3:200#26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r4.claim: Compulsively demanding change in every domain, even where change is unnecessary, is poor judgment.
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r4.anchor: ومجرد وجوب التحول على الإنسان من كل جهة حتى فيما لا يحتاج فيه إلى التحول مما لا ينبغي أن يقضي به ذو نظر وبصيرة

TABATABAI:3:200#26/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r5.speaker: المعترض
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r5.claim: An objector argues that beliefs and universal morals also shift with social settings, eras, geography, class, and ways of life.
TABATABAI:3:200#26/r5.anchor: فالأفكار والآراء تختلف باختلاف العوامل وتتحول بتحول الأعصار بلا شك كائنة ما كانت

TABATABAI:3:200#27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r1.claim: The objection assumes epistemic relativism, making truth, falsehood, good, and evil relative; the author rejects this theory's universal scope as self-refuting.
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r1.anchor: الإشكال مبني على نظرية نسبية العلوم والآراء الإنسانية ولازمها كون الحق والباطل والخير والشر أمورا نسبية إضافية

TABATABAI:3:200#27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r2.speaker: المعترض
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r2.claim: A further objection asks whether laws revealed for life fourteen centuries ago can fit modern cultural and industrial civilization.
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r2.anchor: وكيف يمكن أن تحمل كل من الحياتين أثقال الأخرى؟

TABATABAI:3:200#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r3.claim: Across eras humans retain the same basic needs: food, clothing, shelter, transport, social life, family, trade, industry, and work.
TABATABAI:3:200#27/r3.anchor: يحتاج الإنسان في حياته إلى غذاء يتغذى به ولباس يلبسه ودار يقطن فيه ويسكنه ووسائل تحمله

TABATABAI:3:200#28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r1.claim: Historical differences concern the particular means used to satisfy enduring needs, as elaborate modern foods still serve the same purpose as simple foods.
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r1.anchor: وهذا الاختلاف الفاحش لا يفرق الثاني من الأول من حيث إن الجميع غذاء يتغذى به الإنسان لسد جوعه

TABATABAI:3:200#28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r2.claim: Universal Islamic laws remain applicable as means change, as long as human fitra is preserved without deviation.
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r2.anchor: الفطرة واستدعاء السعادة لا تبطل بظهور وسيلة مكان وسيلة ما دام الوفاق مع أصل الفطرة محفوظا

TABATABAI:3:200#28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r3.claim: Rulers may decide changing, particular policies in public affairs, including war, peace, finance, and administration.
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r3.anchor: فهي مفوضة إلى اختيار الوالي ومتصدي أمر الحكومة

TABATABAI:3:200#28/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r4.claim: Rulers should deliberate with Muslims before deciding public affairs, following the instruction in 3:159.
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r4.anchor: بعد المشاورة مع المسلمين كما قال تعالى

TABATABAI:3:200#28/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r5.claim: These contingent decisions change with interests and causes, unlike the divine rulings in Qur'an and Sunna, which cannot be abrogated.
TABATABAI:3:200#28/r5.anchor: وهذه أحكام وعزمات جزئية تتغير بتغير المصالح والأسباب

TABATABAI:3:200#29/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#29/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#29/r1.claim: The Qur'an explicitly establishes the Prophet's authority and the people's duty to obey and follow him.

TABATABAI:3:200#29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#29/r2.claim: To understand Islamic governance, study the Prophet's life together with the full body of revealed ethics, laws, worship, transactions, and politics.
TABATABAI:3:200#29/r2.anchor: أن يطالع سيرته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ويمتلئ منه نظرا ثم يعود إلى مجموع ما نزلت من الآيات

TABATABAI:3:200#29/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#29/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#29/r3.claim: Many commands about worship, jihad, punishments, and social duties address all believers rather than the Prophet alone.
TABATABAI:3:200#29/r3.anchor: أن عامة الآيات المتضمنة لإقامة العبادات والقيام بأمر الجهاد وإجراء الحدود والقصاص وغير ذلك توجه خطاباتها إلى عامة المؤمنين

TABATABAI:3:200#30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r1.claim: God entrusted the Muslim community's affairs to the community without privileging one member; the Prophet and others share in its social responsibility.
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r1.anchor: فالمجتمع المتكون منهم أمره اليهم من غير مزية في ذلك لبعضهم ولا اختصاص منهم ببعضهم

TABATABAI:3:200#30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r2.claim: The Prophet nevertheless has a divinely appointed distinct role in guiding, purifying, teaching, and leading the community during his life.
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r2.anchor: فهو صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم المتعين من عند الله للقيام على شأن الأمة وولاية أمورهم

TABATABAI:3:200#30/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r3.claim: Prophetic governance differs both from monarchy, which treats public wealth as a ruler's estate and subjects as slaves, and from materialist social systems.
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r3.anchor: وليست هي من الطرق الاجتماعية التي وضعت على أساس التمتع المادي من الديموقراطية وغيرها

TABATABAI:3:200#30/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r4.claim: Materialist societies reproduce exploitation: modern strong nations dominate weak ones as ancient empires did, now in collective form.
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r4.anchor: التاريخ وحوادثه كرت علينا ولن تزال تكر غير أنها أبدلت الشكل السابق الفردي بالشكل الحاضر الاجتماعي

TABATABAI:3:200#30/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r5.claim: Societies founded on material advantage produce class divisions and corruption, unlike the equality intended for Islamic society.
TABATABAI:3:200#30/r5.anchor: لا تخلوا عن وجود تفاضل بين أفرادها مؤد إلى الفساد فإن اختلاف الطبقات بالثروة أو الجاه

TABATABAI:3:200#31/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r1.claim: In Islam, social rank does not determine dignity; the only merit is piety before God and competition in good works.

TABATABAI:3:200#31/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r2.claim: Rulers and subjects, rich and poor, women and men stand equally before religious law and lack social class barriers.
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r2.anchor: فالحاكم والمحكوم والأمير والمأمور والرئيس والمرؤوس والحر والعبد والرجل والمرأة والغني والفقير والصغير والكبير في الإسلام في موقف سواء

TABATABAI:3:200#31/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r3.claim: Enforcement of religious norms is not reserved to a special class; every community member must promote good and forbid wrong.
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r3.anchor: القوة المجرية في الإسلام ليست هي طائفة متميزة في المجتمع بل تعم جميع أفراد المجتمع

TABATABAI:3:200#31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r4.claim: After the Prophet, most Muslims hold that the community elects its ruler, while Shi'a Muslims hold that God and the Prophet designated twelve Imams.
