TABATABAI:3:200#31/r4.anchor: الجمهور من المسلمين على أن انتخاب الخليفة الحاكم في المجتمع إلى المسلمين والشيعة من المسلمين على أن الخليفة منصوص من جانب الله ورسوله وهم اثنا عشر إماما

TABATABAI:3:200#31/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r5.claim: After the Prophet, including during the Imam's occultation, governance belongs to Muslims, who should preserve divine law and consult about contingent affairs on the prophetic model.
TABATABAI:3:200#31/r5.anchor: والدليل على ذلك كله جميع ما تقدم من الآيات في ولاية النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مضافة إلى قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:3:200#32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r1.claim: Islam rejects the role of national and territorial divisions in constituting its community; its social boundary is belief.
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r1.anchor: بنى الاجتماع على العقيدة دون الجنسية والقومية والوطن ونحو ذلك

TABATABAI:3:200#32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r2.claim: Nomadic tribal life and differences in climate and geography gave rise to ethnic and territorial division.
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r2.anchor: وهذان أعني البدوية واختلاف مناطق الأرض في طبائعها الثانوية من حرارة وبرودة وجدب وخصب وغيرهما هما العاملان الأصليان لانشعاب النوع الإنساني

TABATABAI:3:200#32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r3.claim: Separate national communities recreate the fragmentation they seek to escape and treat other societies exploitatively, as humanity treats nature.
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r3.anchor: فتنعزل الإنسانية عن التوحد والتجمع وتبتلي من التفرق والتشتت بما كانت تفر منه

TABATABAI:3:200#32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r4.claim: Islam grounds even marriage and inheritance in shared monotheistic belief rather than residence or homeland.
TABATABAI:3:200#32/r4.anchor: حتى في مثل الزوجية والقرابة في الاستمتاع والميراث فإن المدار فيهما على الاشتراك في التوحيد لا المنزل والوطن

TABATABAI:3:200#33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r1.claim: Muslims must uphold their religion as far as possible in both prosperity and oppression; even an isolated believer must practice what can be practiced.
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r1.anchor: وعليه عند الاضطهاد والمغلوبية ما يستطيعه من إحياء الدين وإعلاء كلمته

TABATABAI:3:200#33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r2.claim: Islamic society can function under every condition: rule or subjection, victory or defeat, visibility or concealment, strength or weakness.
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r2.anchor: قد جعل جعلا يمكنه أن يعيش في جميع الأحوال وعلى كل التقادير من حاكمية ومحكومية وغالبية ومغلوبية

TABATABAI:3:200#33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r3.claim: The Qur'anic permissions concerning coerced concealment and acting within one's capacity support this adaptability.
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r3.anchor: ويدل عليه من القرآن آيات التقية بالخصوص

TABATABAI:3:200#33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r4.claim: Islam makes social organization part of every domain where collective action can serve its laws, including worship, transactions, government, ethics, and foundational knowledge.
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r4.anchor: وصفة الاجتماع مرعية مأخوذة في الإسلام في جميع ما يمكن أن يؤدي بصفة الاجتماع

TABATABAI:3:200#33/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r5.claim: The form of collective participation varies by duty: defense, fasting, and pilgrimage involve groups, daily prayer is individually obligatory, and Friday prayer is communal.
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r5.anchor: الجهة الأولى من الاختلاف ما نرى أن الشارع شرع الاجتماع مستقيما في الجهاد إلى حد يكفي

TABATABAI:3:200#33/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r6.claim: The Prophet warned that he might burn the homes of Muslims who persistently skipped mosque congregation, showing the force he assigned to preserving communal practice.
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r6.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوم من المسلمين تركوا الحضور في الجماعة

TABATABAI:3:200#33/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r7.claim: Although congregational daily prayer is recommended rather than obligatory, Muslims should preserve the Prophet's established Sunna by any available means.
TABATABAI:3:200#33/r7.anchor: فإنها مسنونة مستحبة غير أن السنة جرت على أدائها جماعة وعلى الناس أن يقيموا السنة

TABATABAI:3:200#34/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r1.claim: Juristic deduction from Qur'an and Sunna determines these legal details; the author then turns to Islam's social character in foundational beliefs.
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r1.anchor: وهذه أمور سبيل البحث فيها الاستنباط الفقهي من الكتاب والسنة والمتصدي لبيانها الفقه الإسلامي

TABATABAI:3:200#34/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r2.claim: Islam invites people to innate religion as clear truth, relying on the shared intuition that truth should be followed.
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r2.anchor: نرى الإسلام يدعو الناس إلى دين الفطرة بدعوى أنه الحق الصريح الذي لا مرية فيه

TABATABAI:3:200#34/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r3.claim: God excuses those who lack clear proof or a way to guidance; this leaves room for sincere thinkers to investigate religious doctrines.
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r3.anchor: وهذا يعطي الحرية التامة لكل متفكر يرى نفسه صالحة للتفكر مستعدة للبحث والتنقير

TABATABAI:3:200#34/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r4.claim: Differences in moral dispositions affect understanding; religious education mitigates this by cultivating virtues suited to Islamic teachings.
TABATABAI:3:200#34/r4.anchor: والتربية الدينية تكفي مؤونة هذا الاختلاف فإنها موضوعة على نحو يلائم الأصول الدينية

TABATABAI:3:200#35/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r1.claim: Sin and misguided behavior can instill false ideas, so Islam counters them through ongoing preaching, enjoining good, forbidding wrong, and avoiding corrupt debate.
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r1.anchor: وقد كفى مؤونة هذا أيضا الإسلام حيث أمر المجتمع بإقامة الدعوة الدينية دائما أولا وكلف المجتمع بالأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر ثانيا

TABATABAI:3:200#35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r2.claim: The Qur'an forbids joining those who treat revelation frivolously; worldly attachment causes this irreverence, and education and remembrance are its remedy.
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r2.anchor: ينهى الله تعالى عن المشاركة في الحديث الذي فيه خوض في شيء من المعارف الإلهية والحقائق الدينية بشبهة أو اعتراض أو استهزاء

TABATABAI:3:200#35/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r3.claim: Geographical isolation, limited or distorted teaching, and intellectual limitations require broader outreach and gentle instruction.
TABATABAI:3:200#35/r3.anchor: وعلاجه تعميم التبليغ والإرفاق في الدعوة والتربية

TABATABAI:3:200#36/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r1.claim: An insightful preacher gauges how different listeners receive a message and gives each only what they can understand.
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r1.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن البصير بالأمر يعرف مبلغ وقوعه في القلوب وأنحاء تأثيراته المختلفة باختلاف المتلقين والمستمعين

TABATABAI:3:200#36/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r2.claim: A report transmitted by both Sunni and Shi'a authorities says prophets address people according to their intellectual capacity.
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r2.anchor: إنا معاشر الأنبياء نكلم الناس على قدر عقولهم

TABATABAI:3:200#36/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r3.claim: Every community should send a group to learn religion and then warn its people upon returning.
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r3.anchor: فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم

TABATABAI:3:200#36/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r4.claim: Following the straight path and avoiding other ways preserves the community from division.
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r4.anchor: وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما فاتبعوه ولا تتبعوا السبل فتفرق بكم عن سبيله

TABATABAI:3:200#36/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r5.claim: The “rope of God” that believers must hold together means the Qur'an and its truths, or the Qur'an together with the Messenger.
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r5.anchor: وقد مر أن المراد بحبل الله هو القرآن المبين لحقائق معارف الدين أو هو والرسول صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:3:200#36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r6.claim: Joint study of the Qur'an lets believers resolve intellectual questions through reflection and shared learning.
TABATABAI:3:200#36/r6.anchor: تدل الآيات على لزوم أن يجتمعوا على معارف الدين ويرابطوا أفكارهم ويمتزجوا في التعليم والتعلم

TABATABAI:3:200#37/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r1.claim: Reflecting on the Qur'an, or consulting those who do so, removes disagreements.
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r1.anchor: فأفاد أن التدبر في القرآن أو الرجوع إلى من يتدبر فيه يرفع الاختلاف من البين

TABATABAI:3:200#37/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r2.claim: Referring disputes to the Prophet or authorized leaders identifies the truth believers should follow.
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن الإرجاع إلى الرسول وهو الحامل لثقل الدين يرفع من بينهم الاختلاف

TABATABAI:3:200#37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r3.claim: Islam both protects its revealed doctrines and permits complete intellectual freedom through collective study and investigation.
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r3.anchor: كذلك يسمح للناس بالحرية التامة في الفكر ويرجع محصله إلى أن من الواجب على المسلمين أن يتفكروا في حقائق الدين

TABATABAI:3:200#37/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r4.claim: A believer with doubts should submit them to communal Qur'anic inquiry and then the Prophet or his representative until the question is resolved or disproved.
TABATABAI:3:200#37/r4.anchor: أن يعرض ما عنده على كتاب الله بالتدبر في بحث اجتماعي فإن لم يداو داءه عرضه على الرسول أو من أقامه مقامه

TABATABAI:3:200#38/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r1.claim: Freedom to examine belief does not license spreading unreviewed opinions publicly, which could fracture the community.
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r1.anchor: والحرية في العقيدة والفكر على النحو الذي بيناه غير الدعوة إلى هذا النظر وإشاعته بين الناس قبل العرض

TABATABAI:3:200#38/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r2.claim: Coercively imposing beliefs or suppressing thought through force, takfir, or social exclusion is not sanctioned by true religion; the author associates it with Christian church history.
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r2.anchor: فحاشا ساحة الحق والدين القويم أن يرضى به أو يشرع ما يؤيده وإنما هو خصيصة نصرانية

TABATABAI:3:200#38/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r3.claim: The author laments that Muslims lost intellectual freedom and communal inquiry, adopting church-like practices that fragmented schools and hearts.
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r3.anchor: حكمت فينا سيرة الكنيسة واستتبع ذلك أن تفرقت القلوب وظهر الفتور وتشتت المذاهب والمسالك

TABATABAI:3:200#38/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r4.claim: The true religion is Islam, the human fitra's goal: balanced spiritual, bodily, and social happiness.
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r4.anchor: وهو استواؤه على عرش حياته الروحية والجسمية معا حياة اجتماعية بإعطاء نفسه حظه من السلوك الدنيوي والأخروي

TABATABAI:3:200#38/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r5.claim: Human deviations reflect errors in applying the innate goal rather than a defect in fitra; the goal of creation will eventually be realized.
TABATABAI:3:200#38/r5.anchor: فإنما هو من جهة الخطأ في التطبيق لا من جهة بطلان حكم الفطرة والغاية التي يعقبها الصنع والإيجاد لا بد أن تقع يوما

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r1.claim: Qur'anic passages promise that Islam will ultimately prevail globally; the author rejects claims that its complete governance is impossible.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r1.anchor: فهذه وأمثالها آيات تخبرنا أن الإسلام سيظهر ظهوره التام فيحكم على الدنيا قاطبة

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r2.claim: Islam is humanity's natural collective goal, whether people recognize it or not; historical experience is not required before a social law can emerge.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r2.anchor: أن الإسلام بالمعنى الذي نبحث فيه غاية النوع الإنساني وكماله الذي هو بغريزته متوجه إليه شعر به تفصيلا أو لم يشعر

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r3.claim: Religious laws and material political systems alike arose and endured without prior decisive experiments proving their governance.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r3.anchor: فهذه شرائع نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ظهرت حينما ظهرت ثم جرت بين الناس

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r4.claim: Social systems take hold through resolute commitment and strong-willed people, regardless of whether their goals are benevolent or evil.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r4.anchor: وإنما تحتاج السنن الاجتماعية في ظهورها ورسوخها في المجتمع إلى عزائم قاطعة وهمم عالية من نفوس قوية

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r5.claim: In al-Ma'ani, Ja'far al-Sadiq interprets the commands as patience through calamities, perseverance against trials, and holding to exemplary guides.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r5.anchor: في المعاني عن الصادق عليه السلام في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r6.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r6.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits Ja'far's reading: remain steadfast in religion, resist enemies, and maintain vigilance with the Imam.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r6.anchor: في تفسير العياشي عنه عليه السلام اصبروا على دينكم وصابروا عدوكم ورابطوا إمامكم

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r7.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r7.claim: Al-Kafi transmits Ja'far's reading: be steadfast in obligatory duties, persevere through calamities, and remain attached to the Imams.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r7.anchor: في الكافي عنه عليه السلام اصبروا على الفرائض وصابروا على المصائب ورابطوا على الأئمة

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r8.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r8.claim: Al-Majma' attributes to Ali the reading of ribat as waiting for prayers, since military stationing was not yet practiced.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r8.anchor: وفي المجمع عن علي عليه السلام رابطوا الصلوات قال أي انتظروها لأن المرابطة لم تكن حينئذ

TABATABAI:3:200#39/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r9.claim: The differing interpretations reflect the broad scope of the verse's commands.
TABATABAI:3:200#39/r9.anchor: أقول اختلاف الروايات مستند إلى ما تقدم من إطلاق الأوامر

TABATABAI:3:200#40/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#40/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:3:200#40/r1.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet named complete ablution despite hardship, frequent walks to mosques, and waiting between prayers as ribat that erases sins.
TABATABAI:3:200#40/r1.anchor: إسباغ الوضوء على المكاره وكثرة الخطا إلى المساجد وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة فذلكم الرباط

TABATABAI:3:200#40/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:200#40/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:200#40/r2.claim: The author says this report also comes through other routes and that reports praising ribat are numerous.
TABATABAI:3:200#40/r2.anchor: أقول ورواه بطرق أخرى عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والأخبار في فضيلة المرابطة أكثر من أن تحصى

ZAJJAJ:v1p501/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p501/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p501/r3.claim: اصبروا means persevere in your religion; صابروا means stand firm against your enemy; رابطوا means persist in jihad against the enemy by war and argument.
ZAJJAJ:v1p501/r3.anchor:
أي على دينكم، (وصابروا): أي عدوكم ورابطوا: أقيموا على جهاد
عدوكم بالحرب والحجة،

ZAJJAJ:v1p501/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p501/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p501/r4.claim: لعل expresses hope directed to the believers: they should hope to succeed and avoid acts that would undo their works; the believers described elsewhere have certainly succeeded.
ZAJJAJ:v1p501/r4.anchor: ولعل ترج، وهو ترج لهم، أي ليكونوا على رجاء فلاح - وإنما قيل لهم (لعلكم تفلحون): أي لعلكم تسلمون

TABRISI:3:200/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:200/r1.claim: Ribāṭ originally meant tethering horses against an enemy, then came to mean staying at a frontier post to defend those behind; it also names the tether itself.
TABRISI:3:200/r1.anchor: أصل الرباط ارتباط الخيل للعدو والربط الشد ومنه قولهم ربط الله على قلبه

TABRISI:3:200/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن جريج والضحاك
TABRISI:3:200/r2.claim: They explain the commands as remaining firm in religion, persevering against unbelievers, and guarding the frontier; this means obeying God, avoiding sin, and enduring combat as the enemy does.
TABRISI:3:200/r2.anchor: عن الحسن وقتادة وابن جريج والضحاك فعلى هذا يكون معناه اصبروا على طاعة الله

TABRISI:3:200/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:200/r3.claim: The reciprocal form صابروا suits the mutual contest of the combatants; ribāṭ similarly concerns two sides and preparing horses parallels the cited command to prepare force.
TABRISI:3:200/r3.anchor: لأن فاعل إنما يأتي لما يكون بين اثنين والرباط هو المرابطة

TABRISI:3:200/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r4.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TABRISI:3:200/r4.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb al-Quraẓī distinguishes endurance for one's religion, endurance of God's promises, and guarding against God's enemy.

TABRISI:3:200/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
TABRISI:3:200/r5.claim: Zayd b. Aslam takes the command as persevering in jihad.
TABRISI:3:200/r5.anchor: أن المراد اصبروا على الجهاد عن زيد بن أسلم

TABRISI:3:200/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وجابر بن عبد الله وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
TABRISI:3:200/r6.claim: They explain ribāṭ as waiting for the prayers one after another, since frontier watch was not yet practiced at the time.
TABRISI:3:200/r6.anchor: وقيل إن معنى رابطوا أي رابطوا الصلوات ومعناه انتظروها واحدة بعد واحدة

TABRISI:3:200/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r7.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:3:200/r7.claim: The Prophet says complete ablution in cold conditions, walking to congregational prayer, and waiting for one prayer after another constitute ribāṭ.
TABRISI:3:200/r7.anchor: إسباغ الوضوء في السبرات ونقل الأقدام إلى الجماعات وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

TABRISI:3:200/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABRISI:3:200/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir says endure misfortunes, persevere against your enemy, and guard against the enemy; this is close to the first interpretation.
TABRISI:3:200/r8.anchor: معناه اصبروا على المصائب وصابروا على عدوكم ورابطوا عدوكم

TABRISI:3:200/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:200/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:200/r9.claim: The commands collectively cover duties, avoiding prohibitions, jihad against human and jinn adversaries and the self, defending Muslims and religion, then fearing God in all commands and prohibitions brings eternal success.
TABRISI:3:200/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية تتضمن جميع ما يتناوله المكلف

THALABI:v3p239/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p239/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p239/r1.claim: A Prophetic report promises that a day guarding in God's path places seven trenches between the guard and Hell, each as vast as seven heavens and earths.
THALABI:v3p239/r1.anchor: من رابط يوما في سبيل الله جعل الله عز وجل بينه وبين النار سبعة خنادق

THALABI:v3p239/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p239/r2.speaker: سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
THALABI:v3p239/r2.claim: Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman says the verse was revealed when there was no military frontier post in the Prophet's time; ribat instead meant waiting for one prayer after another.
THALABI:v3p239/r2.anchor: قال: إنه يا ابن أخي لم يكن في زمان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غزو يرابط فيه، ولكنه انتظار الصلاة خلف الصلاة.

THALABI:v3p239/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p239/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p239/r3.claim: A hadith identifies complete ablution in hardship, walking often to mosques, and waiting after one prayer for the next as deeds that erase sins and raise ranks; each is called ribat.
THALABI:v3p239/r3.anchor: إسباغ الوضوء عند المكاره وكثرة الخطى إلى المساجد وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

THALABI:v3p239/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p239/r4.speaker: أصحاب اللسان
THALABI:v3p239/r4.claim: A linguistic interpretation reads the commands as enduring hardship, confronting toil, and remaining in enemy territory without fleeing.
THALABI:v3p239/r4.anchor: اصبروا عند صيام النفس على احتمال الكرب وصابروا على مقابلة العناء والتعب

THALABI:v3p239/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p239/r5.speaker: أصحاب اللسان
THALABI:v3p239/r5.claim: The same interpretation asks believers to avoid fixing their concerns on worldly means and instead hope for joyful meeting with God.
THALABI:v3p239/r5.anchor: واتقوا الله بهمومكم من الالتفات إلى السبب لعلكم تفلحون غدا بلقائي

THALABI:v3p239/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p239/r6.speaker: السري السقطي
THALABI:v3p239/r6.claim: Al-Sari al-Saqati allegorizes patience as endurance in this world, steadfastness as uprightness in battle, and ribat as the reproachful soul.
THALABI:v3p239/r6.anchor: السري السقطي: اصبروا على الدنيا، رجاء السلامة (وصابروا) عند القتال بالبينات والاستقامة

THALABI:v3p239/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p239/r7.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v3p239/r7.claim: One spiritual reading says endure God's trials, contend with His blessings, guard in the enemy's abode, and avoid loving anyone besides Him.
THALABI:v3p239/r7.anchor: وقيل: (اصبروا) على بلائي (وصابروا) على نعمائي (ورابطوا) في دار أعدائي (واتقوا) محبة من سواي

THALABI:v3p239/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p239/r8.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v3p239/r8.claim: Another reading says endure worldly life and affliction, remain in enemy territory, fear the God of earth and heaven, and hope for success in the abiding home.
THALABI:v3p239/r8.anchor: وقيل: (اصبروا) على الدنيا (وصابروا) على البأساء والضراء (ورابطوا) في دار الأعداء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r1.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains ṣbirū as holding to religion and not abandoning it in hardship; al-Zajjāj chooses this interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r1.anchor: قال الحسن (¬2): اصبروا على دينكم فلا تدعوه لشدة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r2.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r2.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the command is to persevere in jihad; Ibn al-Anbārī prefers this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r2.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم (¬4): أي: على الجهاد.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads ṣbirū as be steadfast with your Prophet and ṣābirū as outlast your enemy so they are never more patient than you.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says rābiṭū means remain engaged in jihad against the enemy through war and argument; its original association is horses stationed near an enemy frontier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r4.anchor: قاله الزجاج (¬2). وأصله -عند أهل اللغة-: من (مرابطة الخيل)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains that each side tethered horses at the frontier in readiness, after which remaining at the border was called ribāṭ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r5.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة (¬4): أصل (المرابطة) و (الرباط): أن يربط هؤلاء خيولهم في الثغر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, interprets the command as standing against God’s and the believers’ enemy until he turns from his religion to theirs; most exegetes see sustained jihad in this command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r6.anchor: وكلام ابن عباس -في رواية عطاء- يدل على هذه الجملة، فإنه قال في قوله: {ورابطوا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r7.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r7.claim: Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān says rābiṭū means waiting for one prayer after another; the Prophet’s report from Abū Hurayra calls that ribāṭ three times.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r7.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن (¬2): معنى {ورابطوا}: انتظروا الصلاة بعد الصلاة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r8.claim: Ribāṭ comes from tying or fastening; one who endures something is said to bind his heart or self, so patient persistence in prayer can also be called ribāṭ, as in Labīd’s line.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r8.anchor: وأصل هذا من الربط، وهو: الشد (¬5). ويقال لكل من صبر على أمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn al-Anbārī gloss rābiṭū as stand firm and persist; Ibn al-Anbārī cites al-Akhṭal’s ribāṭ as firmness and constancy, linking it to patience and binding oneself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p273/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة (¬2)، وابن الأنباري (¬3): معنى {ورابطوا}؛ أي: اثبتوا، وداوموا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:197-200/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:197-200/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:197-200/r3.claim: Believers must remain firm in their religion through hardship, or specifically in jihad; they must outlast their enemy and stay stationed in jihad through war and argument.

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r8.claim: A report says patience has three degrees: patience in affliction, in obedience, and in avoiding sin.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r8.anchor: Haberde vârid olduğuna göre sabır üç derecedir: Musibete sabır, tâatte sabır, masiyetten sabır.

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r9.claim: Believers should outdo God’s enemies in patience at trials and struggle, and strive to overcome their own lower desires.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r9.anchor: sabırda Allah düşmanlarıyla yarışıp onların üstüne çıkınız, yani imtihan ve mücahede mevki‘lerinde düşmanların sabrının fevkine çıkmaya ve hevâ-yı nefsinizi yenmeye çalışınız

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r10.claim: Ribat means maintaining mutual attachment to duty, like congregational prayer behind an imam, and especially preparing for war and guarding the borders with horses tethered.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r10.anchor: Ve murâbata ediniz, ribat yapınız, imam ardında cemaatle namaz gibi birbirinize bağlanıp vazifeye mukayyed olunuz

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r11.claim: Ribat originally means binding horses to watch and await an enemy; the term later covers mounted or foot soldiers posted at Islamic border stations.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r11.anchor: “Ribat”; Allah yolunda mülâzemettir. Bu esasen “rabt-ı hayl” yani at bağlamaktan me’huzdur

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r12.claim: In juristic usage a murabit goes to a border station to wait for a period; local residents who live there with their families and earn a livelihood are not called murabitun.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r12.anchor: Istılâh-ı fukahâda murâbıt süğūrdan birine bir müddet beklemek için gidendir

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r13.claim: In contemporary terminology a murabit is a soldier under arms, stationed in barracks or outposts and taking guard duty.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r13.anchor: Zamanımız ıstılâhına göre murâbıt fî sebîlillâh silah altında bulunan ve kışla ve karakollarda duran ve nevbet bekleyen askerler demek olur.

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r14.claim: A report in Bukhari and Muslim from Sahl b. Saʿd says one day of border guard duty in God’s path is better than the world and everything in it.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r14.anchor: Buhârî ve Müslim’de Sehl b. Sa‘d’dan rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r15.claim: A sound-chain report in Ibn Majah from Abu Hurayra says one who dies guarding the border in God’s path continues to receive the reward and provision of righteous work, is safe from the tester, and is raised safe from terror.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r15.anchor: İbn Mâce’de sened-i sahîh ile Ebû Hureyre’den mervî olan bir hadîs-i şerîfte de Resûlullah buyurmuştur ki

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r16.claim: A report transmitted by Abu al-Shaykh from Anas as a Prophetic report says prayer in a border station is worth two million prayers.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r16.anchor: Ebu’ş-Şeyh’in Hazret-i Enes’ten merfû‘an tahrîc ettiği bir hadiste

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r17.speaker: عبدالله بن عمر
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r17.claim: Ibn Umar says ribat is superior to jihad because it protects Muslim lives, whereas jihad sheds the blood of polytheists.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r17.anchor: Abdullah b. Ömer radıyallâhu anhümâdan mervîdir ki “ribât, cihaddan efdaldir. Zira ribât Müslümanların kanını muhafazadır.

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r18.claim: Piety leads to success, fulfilled aspirations, and answered prayers; the ending prayer of al-Baqara is answered in this way.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r18.anchor: İşte Sûre-i Bakara nihâyetindeki فَٱنصُرْنَا عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ duasının da tam cevâbı.

ELMALILI:3:198-200/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r19.claim: Al Imran closes at a meeting point with al-Baqara; al-Nisa begins as a further unfolding of divine upbringing, human creation and brotherhood, family rights and duties, and religious education.
ELMALILI:3:198-200/r19.anchor: Sûre-i Âl-i İmrân hitâm bularak Zehrâveyn bir nokta-i visâlde telâkī eylemiş ve bunun bir inkişâf-ı mahsûsu olmak üzere

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r1.claim: Sabr means enduring pain, difficulty, and hardship; musabara means enduring adversity between oneself and another or resisting an adversary more tenaciously.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r1.anchor: Sözlükte sabır “acıya katlanmak, zorluklara ve sıkıntılara göğüs germek” demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r2.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r2.claim: Razi defines musabara as bearing adversity between oneself and another.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur explains musabara as greater resistance than the person opposing you, such as an enemy.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r4.claim: Ribat literally means waiting and guarding where an enemy may arrive; technically it is staying firm in God's path, watchful and prepared against an enemy, from tying up horses ready for sudden attack, and murabit names a border sentry or soldier on duty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r4.anchor: Daha sonra ister süvari ister piyade olsun, sınır boylarında bekleyen kimseye

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r5.claim: After presenting core beliefs and practical duties such as pilgrimage and jihad, the surah closes with the disciplines needed to fulfill duties: patience for obligations concerning oneself, musabara for obligations involving others, greater resistance in jihad, and border vigilance against surprise attack.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r5.anchor: Yüce Allah kulun sadece kendisini ilgilendiren yükümlülükler için kula sabırlı olmasını tavsiye ederken; kendisiyle başkaları arasında gerçekleşecek olanlar için de müsâbereyi yani kararlılıkla direnmeyi emretmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r6.claim: The Prophet's hadiths urge vigilance against enemies and border guards, promising them great reward from God and rescue from Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r6.anchor: Hz. Peygamber de birçok hadiste müminlerin düşmanlarına karşı uyanık olmalarını, sınırda bekleyerek düşman saldırılarını önlemelerini emretmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r7.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r7.claim: Some exegetes interpret ribat metaphorically as waiting after one prayer for the next, based on a Prophetic saying.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r7.anchor: bazı müfessirler buradaki ribâtı bu anlamda yorumlamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r8.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur says the Prophet's prayer comparison is a simile: waiting for the next prayer resembles keeping watch at a border.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r8.anchor: İbn Âşûr, Hz. Peygamber’in ifadesinin bir benzetme olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r9.claim: The verse can encompass both literal border watch and guarding oneself from evil through prayer; its final command to taqwa joins both, and omitting either leaves taqwa and success incomplete.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r9.anchor: âyetin hakikat olarak her iki anlamı da kucaklayacak mahiyette olduğu kabul edilebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r10.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r10.claim: Abduh defines taqwa as protecting oneself from God's anger and punishment through knowing God and what pleases or angers Him, learned from scripture, Prophetic Sunna, and the exemplary early Muslims; steadfast defense of truth and vigilance lead to salvation and divine happiness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r10.anchor: Muhammed Abduh buradaki takvâ emri ile ilgili olarak özetle şöyle der

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r11.claim: Sources say the Prophet recited the final ten verses of Al Imran when rising at night for tahajjud.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:200/r11.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in geceleri teheccüd namazına kalktığında Âl-i İmrân sûresinin son on âyetini okuduğu kaydedilmektedir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p140/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p140/r1.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p140/r1.claim: Abu Salama says that in the Prophet's time there was no campaign requiring frontier garrison duty; the verse's murabata meant waiting for one prayer after another.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p140/r1.anchor: قال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: يا ابن أخي هل تدري في أي شيء نزلت هذه الآية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p144#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p144#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p144#4/r1.claim: Qatada explains the commands as standing firm against the polytheists and keeping watch in God’s cause.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p144#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وصابروا ورابطوا ﴾ يقول صابروا المشركين ورابطوا في سبيل الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r8.claim: The surah closes with counsel joining worldly victory over enemies to success in the afterlife through patience, perseverance, frontier watch, and God-consciousness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r8.anchor: ختم الله تعالى هذه السورة بهذه الوصاية التي جمعت الظهور في الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r9.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والضحاك وابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r9.claim: They interpret patience as obedience under God’s commands, perseverance as resisting enemies in jihad, and ribāṭ as guarding the frontiers and keeping horses ready.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، وابن جريج: اصبروا على طاعة الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r10.speaker: أبي ومحمد بن كعب القرظي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r10.claim: Ubayy and Muhammad ibn Kaab say ribāṭ means holding firm to God’s promise of victory, waiting for relief without tiring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r10.anchor: وقال أبي ومحمد بن كعب القرظي: هي مصابرة وعد الله بالنصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r11.claim: Another interpretation treats اصبروا and صابروا as synonymous words used for emphasis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p484/r11.anchor: فقيل: اصبروا وصابروا بمعنى واحد للتأكيد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r1.claim: The surah closes by urging believers to hold fast to its guidance and meet enemy stratagems, after recounting rulings, believers’ and unbelievers’ states, and believers’ suffering.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r1.anchor: ختم السورة بما يضوع منه مسك التمسك بما مضى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r2.claim: Sabr means restraining oneself from distress; the apparent command includes the three forms of patience named in a report: through affliction, obedience, and refraining from sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد الأمر بما يعم أقسام الصبر الثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r3.claim: Sābirū means outlasting the enemy in the hardships of war; it follows general patience because it is harder and thus more excellent.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r3.anchor: أي أصبروا على شدائد الحرب مع أعداء الله تعالى صبرا أكثر من صبرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r4.claim: The coordination of sābirū after ṣbirū resembles singling Gabriel out after mentioning the angels, or the middle prayer after prayers generally.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r5.claim: Rābiṭū means to remain at frontier posts, horses held and ready for a raid, surpassing the enemy in readiness; this too is a kind of patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r5.anchor: أقيموا في الثغور رابطين خيولكم فيها حابسين لها مترصدين للغزو

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r6.speaker: سهل بن سعد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r6.claim: Sahl ibn Saʿd reports from the Prophet that a day of frontier duty is better than the world and everything in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r6.anchor: أخرج الشيخان عن سهل بن سعد أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r7.claim: A sound report in Ibn Majah says one who dies guarding the frontier continues to receive his righteous deeds and provision and is kept safe from the interrogators and the great terror.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن ماجه بسند صحيح عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه عن رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r8.speaker: جابر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r8.claim: Jabir reports in a chain al-Tabarani calls acceptable that one day of frontier duty places seven trenches between a person and the Fire, each as wide as seven heavens and earths.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r8.anchor: أخرج الطبراني بسند لا بأس به عن جابر قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r9.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r9.claim: Abu al-Shaykh transmits from Anas, with the Prophet as authority, that prayer in frontier territory is worth two million prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175/r9.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن أنس مرفوعا الصلاة بأرض الرباط بألف ألفي صلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r1.claim: Ibn Umar says frontier duty is superior to jihad because it protects Muslim lives, while jihad spills the blood of polytheists.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r1.anchor: وروى عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الرباط أفضل من الجهاد لأنه حقن دماء المسلمين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r2.claim: Taqwa here means obeying God’s commands generally, encompassing all the preceding commands.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r2.anchor: وأتقوا الله في مخالفة أمره على الإطلاق فيندرج فيه جميع ما مر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r3.claim: Falah means winning one’s aim, attaining the desired goal, and succeeding in one’s pursuit.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r3.anchor: أي لكي تظفروا وتفوزوا بنيل المنية ودرك البغية والوصول إلى النجح

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r4.claim: One elaborate interpretation divides human life into individual and communal duties: patience covers religious reasoning, worship, avoidance of sins, and worldly hardship, while steadfastness covers social forbearance, counsel, and jihad.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r4.anchor: أحوال الإنسان قسمان الأول ما يتعلق به وحده والثاني ما يتعلق به من حيث المشاركة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r5.claim: That interpretation makes ribat discipline the soul’s powers, taqwa guard all action from vanity and ostentation, and falah the divine reward after worship’s duties are complete.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r5.anchor: أمره سبحانه بالمرابطة أعم من أن تكون مرابطة ثغر أو نفس

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi calls the elaborate scheme strained and prefers that the commands form a straightforward progression.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى أنه على ما فيه تمحل ظاهر وتعسف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r7.claim: General patience comes first because it is like the head to the body and the key to relief.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r7.anchor: إنه تعالى أمر بالصبر العام أولا لأنه كما في الخبر بمنزلة الرأس

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r8.claim: A maxim says reason is the human being’s jewel and patience the intellect’s jewel; religious and worldly attainments come only through patience, as the cited poet says.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لكل شيء جوهر وجوهر الإنسان العقل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r9.claim: The second command advances from general patience to jihad, a special patience that brings public benefit and honor; a prophetic warning links abandoning jihad with divinely imposed humiliation until return to religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r9.anchor: وقد جاء عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إذا تركتم الجهاد سلط الله تعالى عليكم ذلا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r10.claim: Ribat is a still higher form of patience: holding a frontier against an anticipated threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r10.anchor: ثم ترقى إلى نوع آخر من ذلك هو أعلى وأغلى وهو المرابطة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r11.claim: General taqwa concludes the sequence because ostentation, self-admiration, and attention to other than God could corrupt the preceding acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p175#2/r11.anchor: لولاها لأوشك أن يخالط تلك الأشياء شيء من الرياء والعجب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra tells Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman that the verse addressed people who maintained mosques, prayed at the appointed times, and remembered God there; patience means the five prayers, steadfastness resisting the self, and ribat remaining in mosques.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r1.anchor: أقبل على أبو هريرة يوما فقال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r2.claim: A report shared by Malik, al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, and Muslim says thorough ablution despite hardship, frequent steps to mosques, and waiting from one prayer to another erase sins and raise ranks; that waiting is called ribat three times.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r2.anchor: وأخرج مالك والشافعي وأحمد ومسلم عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r3.claim: Al-Alusi says the mosque report may be sounder than the earlier report, but its claim that no frontier fighting existed in the Prophet’s time is far-fetched and hardly defensible.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r3.anchor: ولعل هذه الرواية عن أبي هريرة أصح من الرواية الأولى مع ما في الحكم فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r4.claim: Even if sound, the mosque report does not contradict the standard interpretation: the definite ribat can mean frontier duty, while the Prophet compares mosque observance to it as a figure of speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176/r4.anchor: لا تنافي التفسير المشهور لجواز أن تكون اللام في الرباط فيها للعهد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p176#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176#2/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176#2/r23.claim: One allusive reading means patience against sins, steadfastness in obedience, spiritual binding through direct witnessing, and guarding against seeing anything besides God; success is release from worries and thoughts.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176#2/r23.anchor: عن المعاصي ( وصابروا ) على الطاعات ( ورابطوا ) الأرواح بالمشاهدة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p176#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176#2/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176#2/r24.claim: Alternatively, patience belongs to the soul’s struggle, steadfastness to the heart amid manifestations, and ribat to the spirit holding the self against weakness or heedlessness.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p176#2/r24.anchor: أصبروا ) في مقام النفس بالمجاهدة ( وابروا ) في مقام القلب مع التجليات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sunni, Abu Nuʿaym, and Ibn ʿAsakir transmit from Abu Hurayra that the Prophet recited these final ten verses of Ali ʿImran.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r1.anchor: أخرج ذلك ابن السني وأبو نعيم وابن عساكر عن أبي هريرة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r2.speaker: عثمان
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r2.claim: The Darimi transmits from Uthman that whoever recites the end of Ali ʿImran at night is granted the reward of a night’s vigil.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r2.anchor: وأخرج الدارمي عن عثمان قال : من قرأ آخر آل عمران

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r3.claim: Al-Tabarani transmits a prophetic report from Ibn Abbas that whoever recites the surah containing Ali ʿImran on Friday receives God’s and the angels’ blessings until sunset.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r3.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني من حديث إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما مرفوعا من قرأ السورة التي يذكر فيها آل عمران

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r4.claim: Al-Alusi labels fabricated the report promising safety on the bridge over Hell for every verse of Ali ʿImran and censures exegetes who transmitted it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r4.anchor: أعطى بكل آية أمانا على جسر جهنمموضوع مختلق

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r5.claim: Al-Alusi closes his commentary on al-Fatiha and the two Zahrawayn, hoping God will enable him to complete the tafsir through the two refuge-seeking surahs.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178/r5.anchor: و ليكن هذا خاتمة ما أمليته من تفسير الفاتحة والزهراوين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.claim: Nisa is Medinan according to the correct view; al-Nahhas calls it Meccan based on the Meccan revelation of the command to return the Kaaba key, but al-Suyuti says that does not determine the whole surah’s provenance.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r1.anchor: ( مدنية على الصحيح وزعم النحاس أنها مكية مستندا إلى أن قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti argues that a Meccan verse within a long surah, mostly revealed in Medina, does not make that surah Meccan; material after the Hijra is generally Medinan.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r2.anchor: لأنه لا يلزم من نزول آية أو آيات بمكة من سورة طويلة نزل معظمها بالمدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.claim: Aisha’s report in al-Bukhari that Baqara and Nisa were revealed while she was with the Prophet, after their post-Hijra marriage, supports Nisa’s Medinan classification.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r3.anchor: ما أخرجه البخاري عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r4.claim: Another view says the surah was revealed around the time of the Hijra.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.claim: The Syrian count is 177 verses, the Kufan count 176, and other counts 175; authorities differ on whether two clauses are separate verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r5.anchor: وعدة آياتها عند الشاميين مائة وسبع وسبعون وعند الكوفيين ست وسبعون

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.claim: Nisa opens with taqwa after Ali ʿImran ends with it, a strong rhetorical link between surahs known as similarity of endings or tassbigh.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r6.anchor: آل عمران ختمت بالأمر بالتقوى وأفتتحت هذه السورة به وذلك من آكد وجوه المناسبات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.claim: Other links are that Nisa refers to the aftermath of Uhud, follows Ali ʿImran’s mention of the expedition after Uhud, and develops in detail themes stated earlier; this ordering is better than that in Ibn Masud’s codex.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p178#2/r7.anchor: في آل عمران ذكر قصة أحد مستوفاة وفي هذه السورة ذكر ذيلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r1.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r1.claim: Be steadfast in your religion and do not abandon it in hardship or ease.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: اصبروا على دينكم ولا تدعوه لشدة ولا رخاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r2.claim: Patience here means persevering in obedience to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: اصبروا على طاعة الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r3.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل بن سليمان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r3.claim: They explain the command as steadfastness in carrying out God's orders.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك ومقاتل بن سليمان: على أمر الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r4.claim: He explains patience as performing God's obligatory duties.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: على أداء فرائض الله تعالى،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r5.claim: He interprets patience as striving in jihad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r5.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: على الجهاد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r6.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r6.claim: He interprets patience as endurance through affliction; compete in patience against unbelievers and guard against polytheists.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي: على البلاء، وصابروا يعني: الكفار، ورابطوا يعني: المشركين،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r7.claim: He says ṣābirū means persevere and remain firm; ribāṭ derives from tying horses and came to mean anyone stationed on a frontier protecting those behind, even without a mount.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r7.anchor: أبو عبيدة، أي داوموا واثبتوا، والربط الشد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r8.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r8.claim: Sahl reports that a day of frontier service, a place the size of a whip in Paradise, and a morning or evening march in God's cause each surpass the world and all it contains.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r8.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "رباط يوم في سبيل الله خير من الدنيا وما عليها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r9.speaker: سلمان الخير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r9.claim: Salman reports that a day and night of frontier service earns a month's fasting; the reward and provision continue after death and the deceased is protected from trial.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r9.anchor: عن شرحبيل بن السمط عن سلمان الخير أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من رابط يوما وليلة في سبيل الله كان له أجر صيام شهر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r10.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r10.claim: He says ribāṭ in the Prophet's time meant waiting from one prayer to the next rather than military frontier duty; a report from Abu Hurayra calls ablution through hardship, walking to mosques, and waiting for prayer ribāṭ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p156/r10.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن: لم يكن في زمان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غزو يرابط فيه، ولكنه انتظار الصلاة خلف الصلاة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p157/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p157/r1.speaker: بعض أرباب اللسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p157/r1.claim: Some linguists gloss the sequence as patience in ease, endurance in adversity, guarding in enemy territory, and reverence for God, leading to success in the everlasting home.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p157/r1.anchor: قال بعض أرباب اللسان: اصبروا على النعماء وصابروا على البأساء والضراء ورابطوا في دار الأعداء

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r1.claim: Be patient in demanding worship and hardship; compete with enemies in war and with the self against desire, singled out after general patience because it is harder.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r1.anchor: على مشاق الطاعات وما يصيبكم من الشدائد. { وصابروا } وغالبوا أعداء الله بالصبر على شدائد الحرب

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r2.claim: Ribāṭ means stationing bodies and horses at frontiers awaiting battle, and keeping the soul on obedience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r2.anchor: أبدانكم وخيولكم في الثغور مترصدين للغزو، وأنفسكم على الطاعة كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r3.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r3.claim: The Prophet calls waiting for one prayer after another ribāṭ; another report equates frontier duty for a day and night with a month of Ramadan fasting and prayer, interrupted only for need.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r3.anchor: من الرباط انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r4.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r4.claim: A prophetic report promises safety at the bridge over Hell for every verse of Al Imran recited and blessings from God and angels until sunrise for Friday recitation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة آل عمران أعطي بكل آية منها أمانا على جسر جهنم

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r5.claim: Taqwa means disavowing all besides God or avoiding vices to attain patience in worship, self-discipline against habits, and the heart's watch for divine arrivals, called law, path, and truth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:200/r5.anchor: فاتقوه بالتبري عما سواه لكي تفلحوا غاية الفلاح، أو واتقوا القبائح لعلكم تفلحون بنيل المقامات الثلاثة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r5.claim: Be patient in obeying what the two bright surahs call for, including whatever the self dislikes.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r5.anchor: على كل ما ينبغي الصبر عليه مما تكرهه النفوس مما دعتكم إليه الزهراوان

BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r6.claim: Compete in endurance against unbelievers, hypocrites, and other transgressors, so none outlasts Muslims in falsehood longer than they endure in truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r6.anchor: فلا يكونن على باطلهم أصبر منكم على حقكم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r7.claim: Ribāṭ originally means stationing horses at frontier posts to deter and guard against enemies; it later extends to holding a frontier for religion and persevering in worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r7.anchor: ثم صار الرباط يطلق على المكث في الثغور لأجل الذب عن الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r8.claim: God-conscious vigilance is the means of all these duties, remembering as much of God's greatness in blessing and punishment as one can know.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r9.claim: The promised success includes victory over enemies and the bliss of martyrs; the verse states the condition for the plea for victory closing al-Baqara to be answered.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p202/r9.anchor: معلمة بشرط استجابة الدعاء بالنصرة على الكافرين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r1.claim: The close of al-Baqara and this closing exhortation recall God's nearness to supplicants, urging watchfulness in following His signs and opposing His enemies.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r1.anchor: داعية إلى تذكير أولي الألباب بالمراقبة للواحد الحي القيوم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r2.claim: The preceding verses concern believers in all scriptures, including the Qur'an that confirms Torah and Gospel, so God grants victory and punishment of unbelievers at their hands.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r2.anchor: هذا القرآن المصدق لما بين يديه والتوراة والإنجيل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r3.claim: The closing emphasis on God's might and vengeance returns the surah's ending to its opening.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p203/r3.anchor: ردا للمقطع على المطلع على أحسن وجه

DURR-FULL:v2p417/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra says that in the Prophet's time there was no frontier campaign requiring garrison duty, so ribat meant waiting for one prayer after another.
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r1.anchor: أبي حاتم عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه

DURR-FULL:v2p417/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r2.claim: Another report from Abu Hurayra applies the verse to people who enliven mosques: endure the five prayers, restrain the self and desires, and remain stationed in mosques.
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r2.anchor: أبي حاتم عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه

DURR-FULL:v2p417/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r3.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r3.claim: The Prophet says thorough ablution despite hardship, walking often to mosques, and waiting between prayers erase sins and increase reward; this is ribat in mosques.
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r3.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال هل لكم إلى ما يمحو الله تعالى به الذنوب ويعظم الأجر

DURR-FULL:v2p417/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r4.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r4.claim: The Prophet tells Jabir that thorough ablution, frequent steps to mosques, and waiting for the next prayer erase sins; this is ribat.
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r4.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ألا أدلكم على ما يمحو الله به الذنوب

DURR-FULL:v2p417/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r5.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r5.claim: The Prophet tells Abu Hurayra that these same deeds erase sins and raise ranks, and calls them ribat.
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ألا أخبركم بما يمحو الله به الخطايا ويرفع به الدرجات

DURR-FULL:v2p417/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r6.speaker: أبو غسان
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r6.claim: Abu Ghassan says the verse was revealed about remaining in mosques.
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r6.anchor: عن أبي غسان قال: إن هذه الآية إنما أنزلت في لزوم المساجد

DURR-FULL:v2p417/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r7.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r7.claim: The command is to remain firm in religion through hardship or ease, joy or distress, endure the unbelievers, and stand watch against polytheists.
DURR-FULL:v2p417/r7.anchor: في الآية قال: أمرهم أن يصبروا على دينهم ولا يدعوه لشدة ولا رخاء ولا سراء ولا ضراء

DURR-FULL:v2p418/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says endure calamities, remain steadfast in prayer, and perform jihad in God's path.
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في الآية قال: اصبروا عند المصيبة وصابروا على الصلوات ورابطوا: جاهدوا في سبيل الله

DURR-FULL:v2p418/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says endure obligations, stand with the Prophet in battle, and remain committed to his commands and prohibitions.
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في الآية قال: اصبروا على الفرائض وصابروا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الموطن ورابطوا فيما أمركم ونهاكم

DURR-FULL:v2p418/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the commands as obeying God, enduring God's enemies, and remaining stationed in God's path.
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في الآية قال: اصبروا على طاعة الله وصابروا أعداء الله ورابطوا في سبيل الله

DURR-FULL:v2p418/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r4.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r4.claim: The Prophet's instruction is to endure the five prayers, fight enemies with the sword, and keep garrison in God's path.
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r4.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا اصبروا} على الصلوات الخمس وصابروا على قتال عدوكم بالسيف

DURR-FULL:v2p418/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r5.claim: Umar reassures Abu ʿUbayda amid fear of Roman forces that hardship is followed by relief and one difficulty cannot overcome two eases, citing this verse.
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r5.anchor: عمر بن الخطاب يذكر له جموعا من الروم وما يتخوف منهم

DURR-FULL:v2p418/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r6.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r6.claim: The Prophet says one day of garrison duty in God's path is better than the world and everything in it.
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r6.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: رباط يوم في سبيل الله خير من الدنيا وما عليها

DURR-FULL:v2p418/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r7.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r7.claim: The Prophet says a person who dies while stationed in God's path continues to gain deeds until Judgment Day and is protected from the grave's trial.
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r7.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول كل ميت يختم على عمله إلا الذي مات مرابطا في سبيل الله

DURR-FULL:v2p418/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r8.speaker: النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r8.claim: The Prophet says a day and night of garrison duty surpass a month of fasting and prayer; a person who dies there continues to receive deeds and provision and is safe from the grave's interrogators.
DURR-FULL:v2p418/r8.anchor:
رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يقول رباط يوم وليلة خير من صيام شهر وقيامه
